Product: one program draws medieval towns and cities at three rungs — town, city, metropolis — with the size inside each rung set by the requested population, fusing MFCG and FTG step by step plus measured improvements.

Stage plan: stage 2 opens any district as a detailed neighbourhood; stage 3 composes each building of wings and roofs the way Fantasy Manor builds a manor; a separate village generator (thorp → hamlet → village) comes afterwards; the base carries its hooks and does not pay for it.

Ground: a real heightfield in metres with water flowing downhill, so rivers always reach the sea and coasts never contradict contours (neither reference has this; MFCG restarts a city when its river fails).
Demand before streets: from the requested population, our own tables compute counts of houses, workshops, inns, churches etc. and the land they need before any street is drawn (FTG's idea).

Big decisions first: market, castle and large precincts reserved; main roads to gates solved first; first wall follows the town edge measured along them; each gate where its road crosses the edge; moats and canals get a bridge at every gate and crossing; a river is bridged wherever a road crosses it, at narrow places; a walled port has a harbour-side gate its harbour road leaves through; each later wall ring is traced before the streets it encloses grow.
A strip along every wall is kept free of houses and lanes by construction.

Streets: main roads routed over terrain between real destinations (gates, market, bridges, harbour); inside walls lanes are cut by the bent cut (one bend, arriving square to the far side) measured from Neighbourhood's recordings; outside walls side streets grow along main roads as in FTG.

Districts are groups of blocks named for their market, gate, harbour or castle, shaped by a prosperity field rising near centre, market and high dry ground and falling near tanneries, walls and damp low ground.

Plots: every block is divided from its frontage into parcels whose width and depth follow prosperity; rich quarters join plots into fewer larger ones with courts, poor quarters split them and get narrow alleys.

Buildings: each plot gets a site plan (row house with party walls, manor set back behind a yard with outbuildings, detached house, hovel); every building carries floors and roof heights so the optional shadow pass and 3-D export read real heights.
Then towers, castle, bridges, harbour, fields and woods sized to the population, greenery placed by prosperity rules, and names and curved labels that never cover a gate or a keep.
One display list renders the ink look (default, MFCG family), a textured lit look (FTG-like) and a hatched close-up (Neighbourhood-like) on one drawing path.
Exports: SVG, PNG, GeoJSON, virtual-tabletop scenes and 3-D; a large print is made in the background with progress, never holding up the on-screen map.

First picture is always the finished city map, never a rough preview: under 1 s for every town and city and for a metropolis up to about 48 000 people; up to about 2.3 s for the largest (120 000 people), declared for the owner's veto.
values: < 1 s up to ~48 000 people; ≤ ~2.3 s at 120 000

statement: Model build meets the improvement plan's speed bars in 19 runs of 20 for towns up to ~4 500 people, cities ~17 700, metropolises ~59 000, and on every run up to ~3 400, 13 600 and 46 000; larger ones take up to ~0.2, 0.5 and 1.9 s in 19 of 20 runs and up to a quarter longer in the slowest; declared for veto.
At city zoom neighbouring districts are labelled together as named quarters, as many as MFCG labels.

Everything is editable: every element and every rule table; edits are an event list on permanent addresses that survives regeneration and version upgrades; the generator repairs locally rather than re-rolling.

Moving a river or digging a canal lays main roads across new bridges and cuts lesser streets back from the new bank, then puts the water in, changing nothing outside the few blocks it names beforehand, even through a town wall.
The warp brush carries every building outline and roof wing with the ground.

Naming under edits: a rebuilt bridge or street keeps its name; choosing a name list or editing a naming rule renames exactly the names it made after confirmation; a culture street list renames only its streets; a renamed or locked name is offered the list's new name on undo/unlock, for confirmation.
Saved-town load: editable as soon as a sub-second fingerprint check of its saved copy passes; a full re-check from the recipe runs in the background; keeping the saved copy waits for that check.
A town made by a program version the browser no longer keeps opens for viewing only, labelled as made with an older version and not re-checked by this one.
A town kept from its saved copy is shared as its file, never as a link, because a link only rebuilds from the recipe.
Undo works the same when several people share a town and after the file is closed and reopened.

The same seed gives the same town on every machine; adding a decoration or name kind, re-rolling a block or growing the town never reshuffles what exists; a change to an early step changes towns built on it and every release declares such a change stage by stage; edited towns keep edits through permanent addresses.
No whole-map retry: every step that can fail has a short bounded fallback ladder, and the report says for every requested feature whether it was delivered in full, simplified or left out.
The riskiest part (grown streets and bent-cut lanes fitting within the speed budget) is measured first in a spike and again on real terrain and water at the first milestone.

Every acceptance number states whether it checks a rule was followed, compares with a measured MFCG/FTG number, or shows the town is better; the owner's side-by-side judgement follows a written blind protocol at matched sizes; every threshold has a number now; a milestone not yet rated keeps building but is marked provisional and never claims "at parity" or "mastered" until the owner rates or accepts it.
The first product milestone is a viewable town for the owner's eye; editing comes directly after because the owner ranks editability first.

Programmers work from this document and a cleaned research digest, never from references' code, word lists or palettes; every library is permissively licensed so the owner keeps every licensing choice.

Later by the owner's roadmap, with hooks built now: neighbourhood close-ups, manor-style buildings, the village product, sewers and floating islands, evolution over decades, calibration against historical maps, SettlementForge inputs; nothing else is postponed.

The base is one generator making towns, cities and metropolises with one click, at parity with MFCG and FTG and better where the owner asked (terrain and water, streets that go somewhere, plots and yards, smooth prosperity, rule greenery, sensible walls and gates, everything editable, no whole-map retries); a browser library with a small app on top, embeddable later and calibratable against a historical corpus.

Stage table: STAGE 1 base (TOWN → CITY → METROPOLIS; MFCG + FTG fusion plus O1–O19: plot model, granularity, prosperity field, greenery, heights, editability, permanent addresses, layers, drainage, every owner hook, optional @plat/sim content module at its own milestone M4b) build-ready in §2–§14 and §16; STAGE 2 neighbourhood close-ups at interface depth (PART II; base requirements §2.5, §4.12); STAGE 3 manor-style compositions staged by the owner with hooks in §2.6 (outline/compose split, cost contract, intake measurement) and §8.6; VILLAGE a separate product (THORP → HAMLET → VILLAGE) not designed, hooks in PART III and §15.1 VILLAGE-LATER rows; sewers, floating islands, evolution engine beyond the one growth path, corpus calibration (§13.9) and SettlementForge inputs (§11.4 host-input contract) staged by the owner with concrete hooks.
Two ladders: town/city TOWN → CITY → METROPOLIS; village THORP → HAMLET → VILLAGE; they meet without gap or overlap: the village ceiling and the base floor are both 1 500 inhabitants (D-33).

Size within a rung follows population: the requested population picks the rung whose band contains it (lower bound included, upper excluded): TOWN [1 500, 10 000), CITY [10 000, 30 000), METROPOLIS [30 000, 120 000]; roster, stage budgets, district count, frame and plots are computed from the population, never from the rung target.

All three rungs generate from M1 (a rung is a ladder.json row on one pipeline, not a separate build), so M1's goldens, B-CITY runs, determinism tests and diagnostic side-by-side include METROPOLIS; M2b measures and tunes it.

RungProfile (one row per rung in ladder.json in @plat/tables; versioned, calibratable (§7.6), refined by §13.9): rung; populationBand [lo, hi]; populationTarget (the default request); frameAreaKm2AtTarget; aspect [0.5–2, square by default] with side scaling as √(population ÷ target); stageRows: StageRowRef (stage count, regimes, walled shares, §4.2 S2); budgets: BudgetRef (§12.3, §12.5, §12.8); granularity {frontageScale, depthScale, joinMaxDelta by ProsperityBand} scaling §4.7 rows; greenery {parkPer1000Scale, edgeGreenProb, privateGreenShift (points)} scaling §4.9 rows; districtCountLaw, gateLaw: LawRef (§4.5, §4.8); matched {mfcgSize, ftgSize?: BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|METROPOLIS} (§13.6).

Pre-decided fallback: if a rung-modifier ordering fails, the modifier's distance from 1 is doubled once and re-measured; if it still fails the modifier is set neutral (1.0 / 0) and the ordering is reported as not produced.

LadderRouter.route(population) → { product: base | village, rung }: below 1 500 routes to the village product; while no village product is registered the base builds a 1 500-person TOWN and requestedVsBuilt reports the clamp; above 120 000 is clamped to 120 000 and reported; a request naming a rung and a population outside its band is an F-EDIT conflict whose dry run offers the population's rung.

One-click default: generate({seed}) → a TOWN of 5 000 people whose complete city band (every block ground tone, every footprint mass, street, wall, gate and quarter label) is on screen within 150 ms of the click on the reference machine (124–145 ms across §12.2's building range); CITY and METROPOLIS default requests take ≈ 0.33–0.42 s and ≈ 0.86–1.05 s; every size follows §12.5's laws.

Every improvement ships behind the defaults (R8): the fast path never pays for the simulation module, projected shadows, relief, thumbnails or the advanced panel.

Thesis: the references' admitted weaknesses are geometry weaknesses on plain vertex arrays (MFCG 87882877 collapsed edges; FTG 133016301/153121107 hourglass footprints and coincident intersections; 2017 cut() returning its input on ≠ 2 crossings; NG's retries and 42 % silently discarded lot leaves; VG boolean "thorns"); the remedy is one robust planar subdivision — snapped, integer-lattice, exactly predicated, indexed half-edge, typed faces, refined in five nested levels — with every stage a transaction that commits a valid subdivision or is rejected with a typed reason, and everything else derived from it.
notes: Evidence relayed via IMPROVEMENTS.md O3 and proposal-kernel §1.2.

Tiebreaker at every genuine conflict: the owner's DESIGN TIEBREAKER — the approach more faithful to how real settlements are constrained (terrain, water, defence, land use, access, growth) with precise real-unit geometry and measurable statistics, legibility and one-click use as a floor; rows marked TB are where it decided; each criterion carries its §15.2 class C (conformance), P (parity with a measured reference number) or O (outcome the references do not reach).

Discards FTG's destination-less bloom. Criterion: through-roads at a destination 100 % (O4 a, C); detour ≤ 1.4 (O4 b, P).

Secondary streets row (TB): by regime — inside walls S5 grows only district-scale secondaries joining arterials (separation ≈ 120–250 m) and S8's recursive bent cut cuts every lane and intramural secondary; outside walls FTG's staged growth along main roads (destination-aware, curvature-continuous, explicit legality thresholds); suburb regime by preset (§4.4). Discards FTG growth to block scale inside walls and FTG's clamp-only wiggle (15° cap). Epoch: a logged event that runs one more growth stage on the persisted plat: boundary from the one travel-cost field, then the main-road step on the persisted network (S4 re-routes to new destinations reusing streets via their low crossing cost), then the boundary traced as the next enceinte with gates where main roads cross it, then its streets grow; epoch component in every stream key (§6.1); the partition re-derives only faces the epoch touches.

Everything that survives an epoch changes only through explicit logged transformation events — conversions (wall → ring road, gate → junction, outskirt → district) and decline (demolition, abandonment, ruin, shorter wall ring) — each a typed plat operation re-typing edges and faces and re-deriving finer levels locally; nothing that survives is re-rolled.

The evolution engine that schedules epochs from circumstances is staged by the owner; its interfaces (EpochInputs, EvolutionStrategy, ConversionOp kinds incl. decline) are concrete in §4.11; the base builds and tests exactly one incremental path — add a growth stage to an existing town with wall → ring road — at M4 (§16).

Stage 2 in brief: a district is a group of skeleton faces whose boundary edges are typed (shared street with centreline, width and class; wall with gates; quay or bank; field; cliff; sky) and which carries a SeamContract from M1; stage 2 runs a FabricStrategy (base bent cut, or NG ring/square/street templates) inside that boundary at neighbourhood LOD; seams exact by construction (both sides read one shared edge); fields continuous across soft seams.

Village in brief: needs a one-road backbone with partial driveways, detached-in-yard and farmstead site plans, a density field before its roads, a palisade before its roads, and its own ladder with ceiling 1 500 = base floor. Hooks carried now: pipeline = topological order of declared stage IO so a village registers its density stage and palisade (EnceinteStrategy) ahead of its network (§4.1, §4.12); every NetworkStrategy receives traced enceintes; registry admits a tracker-steered network and a houses-along-ways fabric; a village is one district of kind village so building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district holds; class tables include cottage / farmstead / detached; hinterland shared.

Constructive degeneracies (GEO-12) are built on purpose from random parameters because random sampling almost never hits one: a line across a 2²⁴ frame holds at most 2²⁴ of its 2⁴⁸ lattice points, so a random third point is collinear with probability ≤ 2⁻²⁴.

Degeneracy fixtures (geometry classes): lattice points exactly on a segment by gcd stepping (p₀ + k·d/gcd(dx, dy)); collinear triples and collinear overlapping edges (shared runs 1 cm to whole edge, same and opposite direction); cuts through a vertex and grazing a reflex vertex (offset 0 and ± 1 lattice unit); antennae and chains touching a boundary at one point; coincident typed chains (wall on bank, quay on shore, street on district boundary, track on field boundary); rectangles, squares and regular n-gons (n = 3 … 12) rotated and snapped; holes touching the outer ring at a vertex or along an edge and touching each other; simultaneous skeleton events (regular polygons, equal-sided rectangles, symmetric notches).
