The thirteen MFCG asks of §7.4 as scripted scenarios (IMP-16), each reporting its locality share (entities outside the effective scope byte-identical), invariant results and re-run cost against §12.6.

Faithfulness campaign (O9 c; §7.3 item 7 (iv)): New random judged by a nightly campaign, not per sequence — n = 800 regenerated scopes (400 block + 400 district by seeded draw from B-EDIT New-random events, topped up on B-CITY-lite towns when fewer than 400 of a kind), each with K = 50 from-scratch references of the same scope (same upstream state and context, rerolls 32 768 + i for i = 0 … 49, unreachable by user rerolls).

Campaign statistic: for each of four statistics (median plot area, median frontage width, density, attached share) the rank r = references below plus a uniform draw 0 … t over t ties (from the campaign's own stream), exactly uniform on 0 … K for a perfect regenerator; ranks binned into 10 bins ⌊r·10/(K + 1)⌋ with expected counts proportional to rank values per bin; χ² per statistic → four p-values; the campaign fails when Holm's procedure rejects at family-wise 0.01 (smallest p below 0.0025).
Campaign cost ≈ 40 800 scope generations (800 × 51), ≈ 12.5 CPU-min at §12.6's block and district costs (20 400 × ≈ 6.6 ms + 20 400 × ≤ 30 ms), inside the nightly tier budget (§13.8).

Why 800 scopes: with statistics correlated at ρ = 0.8, 400 scopes catch a +0.25 sd bias in only 92.2 % of nights and a 0.8 × too-snug regenerator in 95.2 % (verifier 92.0 % / 95.0 %), first-night detection 0.85–0.91. Executed at n = 800 (docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.py → .out): perfect regenerator fails 1.0 % on continuous statistics (31/3 000 at ρ = 0.8, 15/1 500 at ρ = 0) and 1.4 % (14/1 000) on tied discrete ones; +0.25 sd bias and 0.8 × snug caught in 2 000/2 000 at ρ = 0 and 0.8 (95 % lower bound 99.8 %); 0.6 × snug and 1.5 × loose in 500/500; at ρ = 1 bias 99.3 %, snugness 99.7 %; without the randomised tie-break a perfect regenerator fails every campaign on a tied statistic (fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out).
notes: Rationale + executed evidence; compress to a pointer.

statement: A failing statistic's histogram names the fault: a hump is too snug, a U too loose, a slope a bias.

A failed campaign is re-run once with the next campaign seed (a perfect regenerator fails twice with probability ≈ 1–2 × 10⁻⁴; a fault of the sizes above is declared on its first night with probability ≥ 0.996 at ρ ≤ 0.8, ≥ 0.985 at ρ = 1); a second failure is a regeneration defect entered in known-defects.json, and M3a does not exit until it is fixed (§16), because no threshold can be relaxed without passing a wrong regenerator.

Control sweeps: §7.8's statistical monotonicity and continuity at 21 steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (nightly), METROPOLIS in the milestone tier; the population control's sweep also reports the F-WORK hit rate per stage, which must stay flat across each band.
Option-interaction matrix: every pair of toggles rendered and diffed; no option silently disables another (O12 c).

Documentation coverage (COV-FTG-A25): 100 % of controls and entity kinds have a guide anchor (§14 @plat/docs); every in-app help link resolves (CI link check); the release notes list every open entry of known-defects.json.

Golden suite: 12 seeds × {TOWN, CITY, METROPOLIS} × the four WaterSettings {none, coast, river, coast+river} stores per stage its stage-isolated digest (the stage's new code run on the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs, §6.4), entity counts, the core statistics record and one PNG per LOD and preset; and per shipped preset's label style a per-stop placement digest.

Declared-shift protocol: a release either matches or declares a shift record for every stage whose isolated digest moved (stage, cause — rule-table change, fix, new concern — seeds and statistics that moved, expected direction, output version created) and a cascade record for every end-to-end golden it re-signs (each downstream stage that moved, shown from isolated goldens to have moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated digest moved needs its own shift record).

An undeclared move fails CI; a declared statistic moving against its declared direction fails CI until the record states why; only declared stages are re-signed; stages untouched by a release stay byte-identical (O2 e); a same-seed output change never rides silently (owner non-negotiable 10).
The records are product files (NF-S1): everything the golden gate and the release-notes generator read lives inside plat/, so §17.1 (3)'s path rule and the gate never collide.

WaterSetting = none | coast | river | coast+river — the one spelling of a water setting for B-CITY, the golden store and every record; a seed in a record is a Seed (u32, §2.9) written as its decimal string; permalinks write it in base 36 (§6.4).
values: 4 values; u32 decimal; base 36 in links

statement: ShiftRecord: id; release (generator version); outputVersion (the o<k> it creates, null for a view shift); stage: StageId | S13b | render.stampTiles; cause {kind: table | fix | concern | engine | feature | calibration | baselineShift; ref; note}; seeds[] {seed, rung, water, before, after: Hash128}; statistics[] {metric, rung, before, after, expected: up | down | none | any}; tiles?[] {tile, before, after} (render.stampTiles only, empty seeds list); d5SeedsChanged[]; milestone; date; author.
CascadeRecord: id; outputVersion; upstream (ShiftRecord ids); downstream[] {stage, before, after (end-to-end digests), isolatedUnchanged: true}; seeds[]; date.

MilestoneRecord: milestone; date; outputVersions[] (created during the milestone); shifts[]; cascades[]; parity (path plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json — the ParityReport the exit is judged on, §13.5); d5 {status: D5Status; record: plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json (§13.6)} | null; knownDefects {opened[], closed[]}; exitCriteria[] {id, result: pass | fail | fallback-applied, evidence}.
notes: Open item VS5-3: §17.1 (4) must name record.json among the files entering the product.

statement: Golden store layout: plat/goldens/store/o<k>/ holds per seed and stage the frozen upstream outputs, digests, counts, statistics and placement digests; PNGs content-addressed in plat/goldens/png/ (large-file storage) referenced by hash; plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json holds the shift and cascade records creating o<k>; plat/goldens/shifts/view/<release>.json holds a release's view shifts; plat/goldens/milestones/<milestone>.json is each milestone's exit record.
The golden CLI refuses a record with a missing field; the @plat/docs release-notes generator reads only these files and plat/docs/known-defects.json.

docs/validation/shifts/<milestone>.md and docs/validation/d5/<milestone>.md are research-side copies generated by research/baselines/mirror_records.py (research may read the product; the product never reads research); no CI job reads them; a hand edit there changes nothing.

Placement digests (N-24; §9.1's cross-engine promise): for every golden town, every shipped preset's label style and each of B-ZOOM's 27 zoom stops, S13b places the band's area and way labels for all candidates and the addresses and repeated street names of the default view's visible tiles (§9.2's scope); the digest hashes per candidate in id order the label id, chosen alternate (or yielded), ladder rung, size and every glyph position and angle as exact IEEE doubles.

Placement arithmetic uses only + − × ÷, Math.sqrt and dmath on the fonts' integer metrics and the stop's scale; @plat/labels is held to §6.5's allowlist lint like a model package, and so are the renderer inputs S13b reads — every ObstacleSource and RoleIndex implementation, every function they call, and the S14 code writing the display-list columns they read (bbox, geometry ranges and GeomTable, layer and z, symbol extents from style-sheet sizes) (§6.5 (3), §14); the rest of @plat/render stays outside the lint because its output is pixels compared by visual regression (§13.4).

The PR tier compares placement digests on Node x86 against the store; the nightly tier compares them on all five engines with workers on and off; a digest that differs between engines is a determinism defect and fails the nightly run.

View shift: a placement digest that moves while every model digest holds needs a ShiftRecord with stage S13b and outputVersion null, bumps no output version (placement is view data, §9.1) and bumps the style version of every shipped sheet whose placements moved (the style version carries pixel identity, §6.4).

Stamp-tile hashes (§8.10) are kept with the placement digests; an asset release moving a stored hash while every model digest holds is a view shift (ShiftRecord stage render.stampTiles, outputVersion null) bumping the style version of every shipped sheet drawing stamped classes; an asset that only adds a new class's tiles moves no stored hash and needs no record.

From M1 (LC-19): the output-version stamp, the shift, cascade and milestone records and the stage-isolated golden tooling are built at M1, not at hardening; every milestone from M1 writes its MilestoneRecord (output versions created, shift records, D-5 panel seeds changed) and cannot exit with an undeclared shift.

Preview links: until M4's exit fixes output version 1, every permalink and document made by the app is marked preview — the app shows "preview: made with output version oN; a later release may draw this seed differently and will say so" — and the link carries its o= (§6.4).
notes: Open item VS5-1: §16 M1's reader must open a document of another outputVersion as a frozen view, keeping this preview promise.

statement: Retention of output versions N−1 and N−2 (§6.4) is built and its replay test passes at M3a; from then a link inside the window replays exactly and one outside opens with §6.4's notice.

Nightly cross-platform golden run (Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; workers on and off; pool sizes 0 and 3): identical model digests per stage, derived-complete digests and placement digests on every engine; from M3a the strict GeoJSON of one golden CITY seed (coast+river) with its trees (§8.10 integer-centimetre instance positions, species, crown diameters, leaf types) byte-identical on every engine, workers on and off (§11.1).
notes: §13.2 contract tests use pool sizes 0–3 while this run uses 0 and 3 — different runs, not a conflict. NR4-3 citation is history.

statement: Visual regression: Playwright renders the golden suite per preset, LOD and backend; SSIM / pixelmatch against the stored PNG with a per-preset threshold; the draw-style census of §8.3 per preset; a "no fills" and a "no outlines" render must remain legible (R13).

B-ZOOM (1:50 000 → 1:500, the default view of every rung): legibility floors; no feature pops more than once (footprint hash identical across bands); §8.3's checks — hairline fidelity, decoration stability, role continuity across band switches, no tree mark over a tier-1/2 casing, no casing pixels in junction mouths, the contrast matrix on the rendered city band.

B-ZOOM label checks (§9.4): floors; every node of the city cut (min(N_q, number of districts), §4.5) labelled at or above the floor and within ± 1 of MFCG's 9 / 12 / 18 at the matched sizes; 0 collisions at settled views and through a scripted zoom sweep; the pin-pass fixture (two pins brought together by a warp and two by a rename lengthening the earlier pin's text: 0 collisions at every stop, the later pin reported hidden where boxes meet, placement digests identical after a replay, §9.2); every placed glyph's text/halo pair at the label floor.

B-ZOOM draw checks: the draw-order census (logged (slot, pass) sequence non-decreasing, §8.3); decoration stability for stamped, grid and line classes; reload and two-derivation-order pixel identity of render-time keys (§8.3); §8.5's figure-ground metrics — street-edge recoverability against MFCG's value on its matched plain sweep renders (measured at M-1, §13.5), access-critical ways drawn ≥ 95 %.

Role continuity by family and milestone (VIS-9; N-23): §8.2's rule — every shipped family defines all four bands and mean roof and ground colours move by ΔE2000 < 2 across every band switch — is checked for a family from the milestone that ships its four bands: ink and lit from M2b (M1 ships ink's city and district bands only; B-ZOOM checks that one switch from M1), hatched from M5, ink-family variants from M3b (§16).

App harness scripted tasks (O16 c; IMP-11) on the reference machine of §12.1: share a view link, export a layered SVG, change the coast side, see five variants of one kind, recover from a mistaken regenerate, measure a street with the ruler, find a named building through the gazetteer — each passes when completed in the stated number of UI actions (one where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo) with every app response ≤ 1 s; run on every PR.

Accessibility (COV-FTG-A24): axe-core on every screen and panel of @plat/app reports 0 serious or critical violations; every control reachable and operable by keyboard alone with visible focus; every scripted task also passes keyboard-only; the gazetteer list and search and the "features in view" list reach every building, plot, district and pinned person without the canvas.

Input scheme: every binding of the default keymap.json (§14) fires its action while the map has focus and none fires while a text field has focus; a user-edited keymap round-trips through save and load.

The parity CLI in @plat/testkit reads only baselines.json (our own numbers-only measurements of the references, generated research-side by scripts under research/baselines/ from the captures and committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/) and our B-CITY outputs, reports every metric against its band, and never opens captures/, research/ or reference/.

Baseline: id; metric; unit; reference: MFCG | FTG | NG | VG | corpus:<name> (corpus rows via §13.9); referenceBuild (itch build, FTG server date + create-request hash, NG/VG build — required); capture; script; date; matched? {rung, mfcgSize?, ftgSize?: BIG_TOWN | BIG_CITY | CITY | METROPOLIS, population?}; role: target | weakness | descriptive; values: {p10?, p50?, p90?, n, seeds} | {bins[], histogram[], n, seeds}.
notes: ftgSize here admits CITY, which RungProfile.matched.ftgSize (§1.1) does not — different uses (FTG's timed CITY preset), not a conflict.

statement: ParityReport (written per run by the parity CLI; read by milestone exits, §13.9's CalibrationRun and the release notes): runId; date; outputVersion; generatorVersion; baselines (Hash128 of the baselines.json read); rows[] {metric, baselineIds[], role, rung, preset?, band {lo?, hi?, ksMax?, direction?: above | below, margin?}, ours {p10?, p50?, p90?, ks?, n, seeds}, verdict: pass | fail | reported (descriptive rows always reported), note?}; summary {pass, fail, reported}.
Each milestone's parity report is stored as plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json and named in its MilestoneRecord (§13.3).

The CLI refuses a baseline row without referenceBuild, capture, script or date; a new reference build never overwrites a row — it adds one (id gains the build) and is a declared baseline shift in the milestone's shift record (motivated by VG changing geometry for the same seed between builds 19251041 and 19365073); rows hold numbers, units and provenance only — no names, colours, grammars or code.

⟨M-1⟩ rule (NF-S5): a reference number marked ⟨M-1⟩ is measured by M-1 (§16 lists them); if M-1 cannot measure it (capture lacks the feature, or not reproducible across seeds) the cell becomes descriptive, gates nothing and enters known-defects.json with the reason; the parity CLI reports an ⟨M-1⟩ cell without its baseline row as fail, never pass.

Band rule (DEF-1; IMP-6): target rows pass when ours lies in [p10 × 0.9, p90 × 1.1] of the reference's seed spread (single-value baseline ± 15 %); distributions pass when our KS distance to the reference ≤ 1.25 × the reference's own seed-to-seed KS distance at p90; weakness rows are one-sided (beat the reference in the declared direction by the stated margin); descriptive rows are reported and gate nothing; thresholds no reference can set are §13.7's.

When M-1 re-measures a baseline (five seeds per matched MFCG size, FTG's new captures) the band is recomputed by the same rule with provenance "M-1 ⟨date⟩"; a recomputation turning a passing gate into a failing one is declared in the shift record.

Matched sizes (MN-2): TOWN ↔ MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN; CITY ↔ MFCG size 80 and FTG BIG_CITY; METROPOLIS ↔ MFCG size 130 (FTG per D-31); MFCG numbers from its plain-option size sweep (walls, citadel, plaza, temple on; shanty town, parks, river, coast off; JSON in metres, internal unit 4.00 m).
notes: Matched sizes are stated in §1.1, §13.5 and §13.6 — pick one home.

statement: Curves (FTG-15) are measured after both sides are resampled at a 10 m arc-length step, so neither FTG's 25–40 m placement steps nor PLAT's smoothed vertex spacing enters a number.

Street turning (P): weakness vs FTG (zero mass above 15° per step, flat heading spectrum): no cliff (no empty bin above 15° while the bin below holds > 1 %) and heading entropy ≥ FTG's; target for organic presets: median turning per 100 m within 0.5–1.5 × FTG's ⟨M-1⟩ (a declared exception to the band rule, FTG's ≤ 8 payloads being too narrow); fallback: headingSigma (table value, §4.4) set so the organic median equals FTG's and the growth-drift row re-runs; if drift then fails, headingSigma returns to default, the target clause enters known-defects.json as not met and the row gates on its weakness clauses.
Growth drift (C): net turn of grown streets over 600 m in organic regimes: p50 15–30°, > 90° on ≤ 1 %.

Junction arm angles and degrees (P), every L1 junction: median 85–95°; p5 ≥ 30°; 4-way share organic 0–15 %, ringed 20–45 %, american 40–80 % (NG 361/361 T target for organic; FTG median 90.02°, 58 % in 80–100°, 36.4 % 4-way — weakness for organic, target for ringed and american).

Street runs by class (P): junction-to-junction run lengths per class (never edge lengths) against FTG (main L + 0.5, district (L + 0.5)/2, suburb 30.00 m, lot outlines 14.70 m) — target for extramural ribbon and suburb regimes, descriptive inside walls; class medians by the band rule.

MFCG street signature (MFP-2; P, walled districts, band rule): lot-orientation coherence R4 within 60 / 120 / 250 m (MFCG 0.84–0.97 / 0.58–0.88 / 0.32–0.68); lot alignment with the wall by distance band (within 40 m median deviation 3.5–4.5° and 84–92 % within 15°; 56–70 % at 40–100 m; 38–58 % at 100–200 m); T/Y share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha, lots per block from the sweep ⟨M-1⟩.

Blocks (P): L2 built-block areas per district — KS by the band rule against NG block counts per template at medium ⟨M-1⟩ on the same face shapes (O4 f); FTG block-lot median 441 m² in every class is a weakness (no gradient).
Deep block interiors (IMP-8; P): court share of deep blocks per band by the band rule per class (§4.6) against NG hollow-block frequency ⟨M-1⟩ and MFCG inner-lot removal ⟨M-1⟩.

Bent-cut signature (P) against NG (start at N(0.5, σ) of OBB major axis, σ 0.066 plain and 0.098 ring faces; one bend at mid-course in 380/519; ≥ 85° arrival in 96 %; 53 % filleted): σ within ± 0.02; corner within 0.10 of mid-course ≥ 80 %; arrivals ≥ 85° ≥ 95 %.

Figure-ground and streetwall (MFP-1, IMP-4; O): street-edge recoverability ≥ MFCG − 0.03 (MFCG matched plain sweep renders ⟨M-1⟩); gross footprint cover inside walls reported, expected below 0.60 (MFCG 0.60–0.64 at sizes 40–130, descriptive, direction declared because yards exist); streetwall continuity ≥ MFCG's on dense frontages ⟨M-1⟩.

Plots and footprints (P): ordinary houses median footprint 60–160 m², p95 < 400 m², a sheared minority kept (FTG median 103 m², p95 154 m², quad side 10.3 m, worst-corner p95 22.9° as target; MFCG footprints 225–289 m² are lots drawn as buildings — descriptive, never a house-size anchor).
Entrance rule (P, L4): 100 % on the access edge, 2–4 m (FTG: on the outline, 2.99 m from the road; 53 % of buildings with a vertex ≤ 2 m from a road).
restated_at: §1.4 buildings row ("3 m from the road")
notes: §1.4 rounds FTG's 2.99 m to 3 m — not a conflict.

statement: Party walls and attachment (P, row classes): attached ≥ 90 % in dense/poor; party-wall share by the band rule per class (NG 39–43 % of perimeter, 95–99 % attached — target; FTG residences 0–5 %, industry 96–98 % — descriptive).

Plot-area gradient (C / O): Spearman(prosperity, plot area) ≥ 0.8; Moran's I > 0 (both follow from the rules: C); within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 (§13.7: O) (FTG 441 m² in every class; NG Moran's I −0.04 … +0.03 — weakness).
Alleys (C): alley length per ha by prosperity, Spearman ≤ −0.7 (FTG 0 alley length at every decile — weakness).
Vacancy runs (COV-VG-VN-170; C): share of frontage length in vacancy runs per band within ± 0.02 of the granularity table's share per band.
Quays and substitution (C): quays reachable from the network 100 %; blocks left as substitution residue (F-CUT tier 5) ≤ 5 % of blocks.
Walled share and ribbons (MFP-6; P, band rule): buildings inside the outermost wall and extramural buildings within 100 m of an arterial against MFCG 0.87–0.92 at sizes 40–250 and 71–85 % (sweep).

MFCG anchors (MFP-8; P, band rule; castle in band on ≥ 99 % of seeds): district areas (MFCG 2.4–17.6 ha at size 40, median 29 ha at size 80); wall vertex spacing p50 88 m at size 40; castle 0.5–3.2 ha (8.7 at size 130); plaza 0.32–0.58 ha; 9 / 12 / 18 districts at sizes 40 / 80 / 130.
Outline anisotropy (FTG-5; P): land-sector r90 CV and road / non-road r90 ratio by the band rule against FTG 0.20–0.33 and 1.26–1.65 (target for organic presets); monotone in the anisotropy row.
Block-level use mix (MFP-7; O): residential-only block share, per-block use-mix entropy and trade households at their workplace in §13.7's bands (MFCG's venue mix descriptive).

Towers and gates (P, S7): tower spacing by the band rule (FTG 39 m median, 17/17 towers on ring vertices — target); ungated crossings 0 (FTG 6 and 2 — weakness); main gates = N exact (MFCG 5 / 8 / 12 gates at sizes 40 / 80 / 130); roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates plus a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where placed.
Water (P, L0): outline step ≤ 25 m; width band by class (FTG 50 m resampling, rivers ≈ 31 m mean at CITY — target; MFCG riverWidth 142 m at size 200 — descriptive).

Tree scatter (O): NN p1 ≥ §13.7's canopy threshold; pair-correlation per class reported (FTG NN median 9.7 m, minimum 0.14 m, not Poisson — weakness; MFCG/NG Bridson k = 50 with a 140-point tile — target for the sampler).
Population and buildings (C): requested population within ± 5 % on ≥ 95 % of seeds; the persons-per-building ratio reported (MFCG ≈ 6.12 — weakness; FTG 3.4 — descriptive).

Generation time (MN-2, MFP-5; P): §12.3/§12.5 budgets; model ≤ 2.5 × MFCG at TOWN and CITY and ≤ 5.5 × at METROPOLIS (MFCG app 57 / 131 / 156 ms at sizes 40 / 80 / 130, descriptive with §12.9's declared trade); first map ≥ 10 × sooner than FTG at FTG's timed CITY preset (9 500 people, 2 798 buildings: PLAT TOWN law ≈ 0.24 s vs 6.4–7.0 s) and at BIG_TOWN and BIG_CITY from M-1's captures; NG hood 10–96 ms is the target for opening a district.
notes: See conflict SCOPE-C01 (PLAUSIBLE) against §1.1's rung-table p95 ranges.

statement: MFCG-worst configurations (IMP-5; O): wall-clock p95 per delivered town, ladder costs included, for METROPOLIS with river, coast, walls and castle ≤ 1.0 s (MFCG size 80 with river and coast: 10 attempts for 3 cities, 3.7–4.0 s; 24 restarts in 58 attempts — weakness).
Requested-feature delivery (IMP-5; O): tier-6 omissions of requested features 0; degraded (tiers 4–5) ≤ 5 % (§13.7) (MFCG requested river fails 7 of 10 at size 80; VG discards 4 of 13 highway maps).
Ladder use (C): tier ≥ 2 on ≤ 2 % of transactions per stage; p99 ≤ 3 attempts.

Draw style (IMP-15, VIS-16; P): ink — casing law on 100 % of ribbons, round joins ≥ 99.9 %, order parity as §8.3 defines, widths ± 15 %, outline share ≤ 25 % (MFCG casing = core + 2h on 7/7 maps, round joins 4 062/4 063, 17-step order, wall/tower/road-core 6.2/12.4/6.5 px at size 40); hatched — 15–20 triangles per wing, no ridge stroke, outline = footprint (NG ≈ 17.4 triangles, 2.33 shadow quads per wing); our roof law within ± 0.02 and our water bands W · (i / N)^1.5 within 1e-4 (NG roof ratios 0.787/0.802/0.834 and VG water bands 5.196 : 2.828 : 1 descriptive).

Labels (O): protected overlaps 0; inside-area share ≥ 99 %; curvature within §13.7's limit; 0 labels crossing holes; count per the anchors row (MFCG covers gates and the keep and straddles walls — weakness).

Between-seed variety (IMP-12; O): dispersion of the §7.7 signature vector (radial share of arterials, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share, outline anisotropy) over 100 seeds per rung and water setting — mean pairwise distance of rung-standardised vectors — ≥ the larger of MFCG's and FTG's dispersion at the matched rung ⟨M-1⟩.

"Mastered" = the owner's eye on side-by-sides against MFCG and FTG at town, city and metropolis plus the measured parity numbers (D-5); the protocol makes the eye a recorded, repeatable judgement that cannot be steered by seed choice and never lets a milestone claim the eye's verdict without the eye.

When: M1 (diagnostic — recorded, not gating; covers all three rungs), M2b (gates "the base at parity"), M4 (gates "mastered"), M5 against NG (gates stage 2, replacing S2's blind preference test with n ≥ 20 raters, for which the program has no pool; IMP-11).
Seeds fixed before rendering: every pair's seeds come from a formula and are committed before any render; no seed is replaced after rendering; every list is reproducible from its formula.

H32(s) = the first 32-bit output word (h1) of MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit (the algorithm §6.2's H128 implements) over the UTF-8 bytes of s with seed 0; it passes the published verification value (SMHasher procedure 0xB3ECE62A); the result is a u32 Seed (§2.9) written in records as its decimal string.

plat d5 seeds ⟨milestone⟩ (product CLI) writes the milestone's pair list (one D5Pair per pair) to plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/seeds.json before any render; besides the formulas it reads only the two numbers-only files the research-side panel script commits beside it — ftg-captures.json (M1, M2b, M4) and ng-counts.json (M5) — never captures/ (§17.1 (3), (4)); ⟨milestone⟩ ∈ M1, M2b, M4, M5; ⟨rung⟩ a Rung; ⟨water⟩ a WaterSetting; ⟨i⟩, ⟨k⟩ decimal.
notes: Open item VS5-3: §17.1 (4) must also name the sitting's record.json as a product input.

statement: Against MFCG (M1, M2b, M4): five pairs per rung and per water setting (none; coast+river), ten per rung; PLAT seed H32("d5/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨water⟩/⟨i⟩"), i = 0 … 4 (check vectors: "d5/M1/TOWN/none/0" = 1221236157; "d5/M1/TOWN/coast+river/4" = 3998735106); MFCG seed from the same formula with prefix d5-mfcg/, reduced as 1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646) into 1 … 2³¹ − 2 (MFCG's Park–Miller state range; check vector d5-mfcg/M1/TOWN/none/0 → 1965791931) by the research-side panel script; MFCG draws none with plain options and coast+river with river and coast on.

Against FTG (M1, M2b, M4; TOWN and CITY, METROPOLIS per D-31): FTG cannot be seeded, so one pair per FTG capture at the matched size (BIG_TOWN for TOWN, BIG_CITY for CITY), each used once in capture order — three pairs per rung; M-1 takes per size three captures with water options nearest none (one) and coast+river (two), recording each capture's id (folder under captures/ftg/), WaterSetting and recorded population (residents in its decoded payload) in the capture README (§16).

At each FTG milestone the research-side panel script writes plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/ftg-captures.json (one FtgCapture per capture, capture order, ids and numbers only) and commits it like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)) before plat d5 seeds runs; PLAT's side is generated at the capture's recorded population and WaterSetting from that file with seed H32("d5-ftg/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨capture id⟩"), so every milestone pairs the same captures at the same populations with its own PLAT seeds.

FTG capture fallback: a capture whose payload yields no resident count takes its size's nominal target (BIG_TOWN 5 600, BIG_CITY 24 500), marked populationSource: nominal and reported; a population outside the rung's band (§1.1) is clamped into the band and the clamp reported; the capture file and seed list are committed before any PLAT render.

Against NG (M5): NG is seedable (MINSTD), so five pairs per NG template for the four templates PLAT registers as fabrics — area, street, square, ring (II.2) — twenty pairs; NG seed H32("d5-ng/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩"), i = 0 … 4, reduced as 1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646) into 1 … 2³¹ − 2 (check vectors d5-ng/M5/area/0 → 1819777585; d5-ng/M5/ring/4 → 951122398), generated at NG's medium size by the research-side panel script, which counts each hood's buildings; counts reach the product as numbers only in plat/goldens/d5/M5/ng-counts.json, committed like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)).
notes: Open item VS5-2: "area" is not a FabricStrategyId — PLAT's side for area must be the district's own bent-cut fabric opened as a refine close-up.

statement: NG pair PLAT side: one district of a PLAT town opened with the same template at neighbourhood LOD (setAttr(district.fabric, template), II.4) in the template's default form (square: SquareFabric void mode); found by a committed search — town k = 0 … 31 generated with seed H32("d5/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩/⟨k⟩") (check "d5/M5/area/0/0" = 3881605733), water none, population ⌊min(50 000 × 1.25^⌊k/4⌋, 120 000)⌋ (four towns each at 50 000, 62 500, 78 125, 97 656, the rest at the cap); in each town the district whose city-LOD building count is nearest the NG hood's (ties to the smaller address id) is opened, and the first whose opened count lies within ± 20 % of the hood's is the pair's; k, the district address and both counts are committed with the seeds.
notes: VS5-2 required change: for area, no setAttr — refine close-up of bent-cut; street/square/ring via setAttr, a replace close-up.

statement: NG search fallback: a pair with no district within ± 20 % after k = 31 takes the nearest-count of the 32 opened districts, marked sizeMismatch; the ratio is printed on the sealed key and reported beside the verdict; the pair is rated like any other; the search's k and each pair's count ratio are reported with the panel (measurement at M5).

Matched pairs: each MFCG/FTG pair shows PLAT and one reference at the same rung, ground scale (metres per pixel) and frame; against MFCG PLAT's population is set so its building count matches MFCG's at sizes 40 / 80 / 130 (§12.2's rate); against FTG PLAT uses the capture's recorded population (near BIG_TOWN 5 600 and BIG_CITY 24 500) and water from ftg-captures.json; against NG each side fills the same frame (NG rescales its hood), so size is matched by building count, not metres per pixel.

Looks per reference: PLAT draws ink against MFCG's default style, lit against FTG's default from M2b (ink at M1), hatched against NG's (M5); against FTG the pair of each rung's first capture shows the extramural suburb at FTG's overview framing (both sides alike, VIS-3); the other two use the matched frame.

Blind order: generator-identifying furniture (titles, legends, compasses, interface chrome) removed from both sides; blind pairs rendered without labels, labels judged in a separate non-blind pass; left/right a seeded coin per pair, pair order shuffled; the key sealed (only its hash committed) and opened after the answers.

Rubric: three questions per pair, each answered left, right or same with an optional one-line note — (1) Legibility (which lets you read streets, walls and quarters more easily at this size), (2) Realism (more like a real medieval town), (3) Charm (rather use for a game or story).

Pass rule: per reference and question PLAT judged better or same on ≥ ⌈2n/3⌉ of that reference's pairs, counted per group — MFCG over the milestone's MFCG pairs (20 of 30 with all rungs rated), FTG per rung (2 of 3 per rung and question), NG over its twenty (14 of 20) — and in no rung (MFCG) or template (NG) is PLAT judged worse on every pair; a gating milestone whose rated run fails a question does not exit until a re-run passes or the owner accepts the failure in the record; the failing question and owner notes enter known-defects.json.

Rater and unrated panel (NF-S2): the owner is the declared rater, no seat rates on the owner's behalf; if unrated within seven days of the panel being ready, the build continues on measured numbers and the D-5 status is recorded provisional — not rated in its D5Record and MilestoneRecord; a provisional status never claims what the panel gates (M2b "the base at parity", M4 "mastered", M5 stage-2 gate), which only a rated pass or an owner acceptance recorded in the D5Record can claim.
restated_at: §16 M2b / M4 / M5 exit cells (SCOPE-460, SCOPE-467, SCOPE-469)

statement: The same panel (same seeds, re-rendered under the current output version) is offered again at every later milestone and, after M5, with every release, until rated; a later rated pass sets passed with its date; a later rated failure follows (6); the release notes state every provisional status (§14 @plat/docs); §16 states the same rule at each gating exit.
notes: Explicitly restated in §16 at each gating exit.

statement: Threshold panel: at the same sitting the owner sees §13.7's strips (one seed at a threshold's number and one step either side) and picks one or answers same; the pick becomes the threshold with provenance "owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩".

house pick: from M4 the sitting also shows the three candidate house sheets drafted at M3b (D-1) on the milestone's seeds; if no house pick is recorded by M4's exit, candidate 1 (first in M3b draft order) ships as house, selectable and never the default; ink stays the default; the pick is offered again at every later sitting and a later pick replaces house's sheet as a style-version change (pixels only; no model digest moves).

Record and clean room (NF-S1): the panel is assembled research-side (research/d5/) from PNG exports the product CLI writes and from reference images in captures/; the product never reads the captures (§17); the machine-readable record lives in the product, committed by the seat that ran the sitting like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)) — numbers, hashes and answers only, no reference image or data.
notes: Open item VS5-3 (conflict SCOPE-C02): §17.1 (4) says the only product inputs are two numbers-only files.

statement: D5Status = diagnostic (M1) | passed | failed | accepted (failure or unrated panel accepted by the owner in writing) | provisional-not-rated.

D5Pair (one per pair in seeds.json and the record, in (2)'s order): MFCG {rung, water: none | coast+river, i, platSeed, refSeed (1 … 2³¹ − 2)}; FTG {rung: TOWN | CITY, capture (folder name), water, population (from its FtgCapture), populationSource: recorded | nominal, platSeed, suburbFrame}; NG {template: area | street | square | ring, i, refSeed, k, platSeed, population, district (address id), buildings {ref, plat}, sizeMismatch}.
notes: VS5-2: add the area → bent-cut mapping in the NG comment.

statement: FtgCapture = {capture, rung: TOWN | CITY, water, population (decoded residents or nominal target), populationSource: recorded | nominal}; the file plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/ftg-captures.json is FtgCapture[] in capture order, research-side, numbers and ids only.

D5Record (plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json): milestone; status; date; offeredAgainAt[]; pairs: D5Pair[] (seeds as decimal strings); platImages: Hash128[] (PNG hashes of PLAT's side in pair order); key {commitment: Hash128, revealed?}; answers[] {pair, question: legibility | realism | charm, answer: left | right | same, note?}; verdicts[] {reference, question, group: all | Rung, betterOrSame, pairs, needed (⌈2n/3⌉), worseOnEveryPairInARungOrTemplate, pass}; thresholdPicks[] {letter, picked: number | same}; houseSheet?; acceptance? {by: owner, text, date}.
The research-side docs/validation/d5/⟨milestone⟩.md (human-readable, with reference image hashes) is generated from record.json (§13.3); no CI job reads it.

Every threshold is in exactly one of two classes: reference-settable bands (§13.5, set by its band rule from baselines.json) or thresholds no reference can set (listed in §13.7) — each of the latter has a number now (provenance "architecture 2026-09-25"), is confirmed at the first milestone at which its mechanism runs, and has a pre-decided fallback; the corpus phase may later re-sign any as a declared shift (§13.9).

J-T, the calibration rule every table row and threshold cites (NF-S4): every value has a number now and a provenance (§17.1 (6)); a reference-settable value is set from baselines.json by §13.5's band rule; any value may later be re-signed only by a declared shift (M-1 re-measurement, owner pick on §13.6 (8)'s panel, calibration run §13.9); no acceptance run treats an unset value as passed — a table with an empty cell fails to load; §4.7's granularity table, §4.9's greenery table and §13.7 cite it as "J-T".
notes: J-T is a rule id living in §13.7, not in the Judgment calls list — keep here.

statement: Fallbacks that move a threshold (NF-S5): a fallback may change a mechanism (table value, weight, radius) and re-measure against the same threshold; a fallback that instead moves the threshold to a measured value is marked not achieved — the letter and measured value enter known-defects.json, the parity report and release notes, and are never cited as evidence an improvement was achieved (§15.2 O class); an owner pick on the threshold panel is not a fallback but the owner setting the number (provenance "owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩").

O18 (i) smooth field: p99 of |∇P| ≤ 0.5 per 100 m of the normalised prosperity field outside hard seams; confirmed M2b (B-CITY and a §13.6 strip at σ = 45 / 60 / 90 m); fallback σ rises one step (60 → 75 m) and re-measures; an owner pick of σ sets σ and the threshold is re-signed at that σ's measured p99 ("owner-eye").

O18 (j) plot-size variety: within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 for districts with ≥ 30 plots; M2b; fallback: granularity rows' frontage CV rises 0.25 → 0.35 and re-measures; if still failing the floor becomes the measured p10 — not achieved.
notes: §13.5 restates the CV floor without the ≥ 30-plot qualifier.

statement: O18 (h), O7 (f), S3 soft seams: across soft seams Δ median frontage ≤ 25 %, Δ median plot area ≤ 35 %, Δ median storeys ≤ 1; M2b; fallback: seam smoothing radius doubles and re-measures; if still failing the band becomes measured p95 + 5 points — not achieved.

O19 (d) canopy: tree nearest-neighbour p1 ≥ 0.5 × the class's mean crown diameter (orchard, avenue, garden), ≥ 0.3 × for woods; M2b (bench, §8.10's stamps); fallback: the class's stamp spacing range (table value, §4.9) raised until its lower end meets the threshold (scaled tiles' minimum distance is the entity's own spacing, so the shipped asset does not change).

O19 (g) city-zoom greenery: every green face ≥ 0.3 ha drawn at the city band with a short side ≥ 2 px; green/ground and green/paper pairs at or above §8.2's contrast floors; no option coupling drops the layer; M2b for ink and lit (the milestone building S12's greenery rules); fallback: the green role steps one value step from ground (style row) and re-checks.
O12 (a) legibility floors: minimum drawn feature ≥ 2 px; area-label cap height ≥ 7 px (§9.4); M1 (B-ZOOM and a §13.6 strip at 6 / 7 / 8 px); fallback: the owner's pick, with no pick 7 px stands.
O13 (a) label curvature: a label's spine turns ≤ 45° over any window of the label's length (§9.3); M1; fallback: the spine's smoothing step doubles; a label still over takes §9.4's next ladder rung.

O13 (c) name–feature consistency: a name referencing a feature type has that feature within 250 m; M1; fallback: the grammar's feature guard shrinks its radius 250 → 200 m and re-measures against 250 m.
O7 (b) water-dependent trades within 100 m of water; M2b; fallback: the placement score's water term weight doubles.

O14 (b) farmsteads: every farmstead within 300 m of one of its own fields and within 1 500 m of all; M2b; fallback: the hinterland unit's S10 re-sites a violating farmstead to its fields' area-weighted centroid (§4.9).

O14 (c) wood edges: edge straightness (chord ÷ path over 200 m windows) median ≤ 0.90; canopy fraction monotone in the wildness control; M3b; fallback: edge-noise amplitude rises by half and re-measures.

O14 (e) built / map area: settlement-perimeter area ÷ frame area (without margin) within 0.06–0.25 at every rung and population; M1; fallback: the frame side per rung is rescaled in ladder.json so the median ratio is 0.12 (a declared shift).

Block-level use mix (MFP-7): residential-only blocks ≤ 60 % in core districts; per-block use-mix entropy p50 ≥ 0.5 bits; ≥ 70 % of trade households live at their workplace; M2b; fallback: the live-in default share of craft and shop rows rises one step (§10.2).

Requested features (IMP-5): degraded delivery (tiers 4–5) on ≤ 5 % of requested features; M1; fallback: the F-* ladder whose degraded rung fires most gets 5 instead of 3 tier-3 attempts and re-measures; if still over, the band becomes the measured rate + 2 points and the top three causes enter known-defects.json — not achieved.

O16 (c) scripted tasks: one UI action where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo; every app response ≤ 1 s; confirmed M1 (link, SVG, coast side, variants), M2a (undo), M3b (the rest); fallback: a task over its action count gets a toolbar shortcut and repeats.

O2 (c) carry-over: edited entities kept or carried ≥ 95 % for local actions and re-derivation from S7 on, ≥ 80 % from S4–S6, ≥ 60 % from S1–S3 (§15.2); M3a (B-EDIT); fallback: §6.3's doubled anchor radii with the IoU test, then an edited building or plot without a successor re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint.

S4 (d) square area (stage 2): typed squares (market, church forecourt, well square, bridgehead, crossroads) inside a district: 0.03–0.15 ha per 1 000 inhabitants over districts of ≥ 1 000 inhabitants; M5; fallback: square-sizing rows scaled so the median is 0.08 ha per 1 000 (declared shift) and re-measures.

Realism against real towns is measured by the corpus phase (§13.9), staged by the owner after the standalone generators; until then the base's realism evidence is the D-5 realism question and §13.5's P rows, and §15.2 says so.

Full verification rig ≈ 10–20 CPU-hours (12 000 B-CITY generations ≈ 1.6 CPU-h before the suite; 10⁵ oracle regenerations ≈ 8 CPU-h; 10⁶ fuzz inputs × ≈ 20 primitives ≈ 0.3–5.5 CPU-h), so it cannot gate a single change; three tiers each with a wall-clock budget on a stated runner (16-core x86-64 Linux; timings normalised by §12.1's calibration score).

PR tier (every change, ≤ 15 min on 8 cores): lint (determinism allowlist, units, dependency direction, repository path rule), type check, unit and contract tests; B-FUZZ 10⁴ random inputs per primitive + the whole constructive set; B-CITY-lite 50 seeds per rung × 4 water settings; B-EDIT 10³ sequences with the oracle once per sequence; stage-isolated goldens and placement digests on Node x86; every style sheet through §8.2 slot resolution at every band (0 unresolved, 0 ambiguous) and render keys across two B-CITY-lite seeds per rung; stamp-tile loaded hashes and seam check; licence, notices and deny-list scans; app scripted and accessibility tasks on Chromium.

Nightly tier (≤ 4 h on 16 cores): B-CITY 1 000 seeds × 4 water × 3 rungs with the invariant suite and §12.3's max-clause screen; B-FUZZ 10⁶ per primitive; B-EDIT 10⁴ sequences; the O9 (c) faithfulness campaign (800 × 50, ≈ 12.5 CPU-min); the five-engine golden run (one PNG per LOD and preset, placement digests, stamp-tile asset rebuilt on five engines and loaded hashes in both workers, sliced-raster and sliced-placement census rows) and from M3a the five-engine GeoJSON with trees; visual regression and B-ZOOM; control sweeps at TOWN and CITY; option matrix; B-REF parity report.

Timing phase: last and alone on the nightly runner (§12.1; ≤ 20 min): cost-model sweeps (nine sizes × five seeds with the F-WORK flatness check), first-map runs at the same three sizes per rung (§12.5), model budgets re-measured inside Chrome's worker on the same seeds (the Chrome figure governs a gap above ± 15 %, §12.1), and re-timing of the max clause's flagged generations (§12.3).

Milestone tier (every milestone exit and weekly; ≤ 12 h on 16 cores): B-EDIT 10⁵ sequences; METROPOLIS control sweeps; the 20-epoch test; the parity report at five seeds per matched size; the D-5 renders incl. every earlier panel still provisional — not rated (§13.6 (7)); §12.3's pool comparison in the timing phase at every rung the milestone confirms; memory and document-size tests at every rung.

A tier whose normalised wall-clock exceeds its budget by more than 10 % fails with over budget; the answer is to split the job or make it faster, never to raise the cap — a budget changes only by a recorded decision; measurement at M0: the harness times each tier; fallback: if the PR tier exceeds 15 min, B-CITY-lite drops to 25 seeds per rung and random fuzz to 5 × 10³ inputs per primitive (the constructive set is never cut) and the nightly tier absorbs the difference.

Corpus calibration is staged by the owner after the standalone generators (base, neighbourhoods, buildings, village); the corpus lies outside this folder and is not read by this program; the base carries the interface now so the corpus phase needs one adapter and no other code.

CorpusAdapter {id, version, maps(): AsyncIterable<CorpusMap>} (written in the owner's staged phase); CorpusMap {id, source (archive, sheet, date), era, region, populationEstimate?, features: FeatureCollection — GeoJSON in metres: ways, blocks, plots, buildings, walls, water, greens with kinds}; CalibrationRun {id, corpus {adapter, version, maps[]}, metrics[] (§13.5 ids, same parity code), changes[] {table, rowKey, column, from, to, evidence[] (baseline ids)}, before, after: ParityReport, shifts: ShiftRecord[] (cause.kind calibration)}.

Calibration steps: (1) parity code computes every §13.5 metric on the adapter's maps research-side and writes baselines.json rows with reference corpus:⟨map id⟩, role target, referenceBuild = corpus version; (2) a CalibrationRun changes table cells only — every cell is {value, unit, provenance, calibratable} (§7.6) and each changed cell's provenance becomes {source: corpus, evidence, date}; (3) the run ships as a table-version bump inside an output-version bump with a shift record per moved stage (§13.3, §6.4) in plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json with the run id as cause, so every existing document replays under its own output version; (4) first re-signed: era and region presets (D-2), rung profiles (§1.1), granularity, site-plan and greenery rows (§4.7, §4.9), forms' signatures (§7.7), and §13.7 thresholds with provenance architecture or owner-eye where the corpus measures them.

Packages have one-way dependencies: the kernel knows nothing about towns, the model nothing about drawing, the drawing code nothing about how the town was made; the app sits on a headless library; new looks, templates, export formats, building generators and rule tables plug into named registries without touching the pipeline; everything lives in one repository plat/ that never reads research material (§17).

@plat/kernel: lattice, predicates, one arena per layer with the five levels as views (§2.2), role and owner tables, stored-reference resolution, batched transactions, kernel invariants, arrangement booleans/buffers/bands (§3.7), straight skeleton and validator (§3.8), obb/hull/lir, delaunay (delaunator), poisson (stamped ranked tiles built from a constant stream key at build time by plat/tools/stamptiles/, in a worker only as the fallback rebuild, §8.10), curves, index (flatbush / rbush / grid), noise, dmath (fdlibm 5.3 port), rng (xoshiro + 128-bit keys; rng.stream the one structured stream mixer of §6.1), concern registry.

@plat/model: schema (zod), addresses and lineage (§6.3), layers, entity registry (CI path-coverage test), lifecycle, provenance, document, serialisation (.plat, CBOR twin), migrations, Merkle model digest, core statistics record, control registry; label records LabelEntity and QuarterNode (§9.1) and the shared view vocabulary LodBand, Role, ZoomStop.
notes: Open item NR5-2: add the LabelRows view here (beside LodBand, Role, ZoomStop).

statement: @plat/tables: rule tables, presets, style sheets, rung profiles (ladder.json, §1.1), work-limit coefficients (workLimits.json, §5.1 (5)), setting packs (§10.4) and the default keymap as versioned JSON with provenance; loaders; the override layer.
@plat/site: S1 terrain, hydrology, coast/lake/island outline routine, rivers by descent, islands, bank classes, water faces.

@plat/content: S2 sequential roster, demand, government and religion rows, S7b/S10a allocation, S10b placement, households and people derivation, relation-store schema, economy and personality schema stubs (D-32), naming engine + grammar.

@plat/layout: S3 siting, reservations and gate sites, S4 backbone, S5 growth and regimes, S6 grower/typing/fields/quarter merge tree, S7 fortification and water furniture, S7b claims, S8 infill (BentCutFabric), S9 corridors, S12a hinterland siting, the hinterland unit, S12b greenery; the StrategyRegistry and the ordering of registered StageDecls.

@plat/plots: S10 granularity law, per-frontage regions, joins/splits/alleys, boundary treatments; S11 site plans, packer, heights, footprint templates; the BuildingGenerator interface (outline / compose) + OutlineBuildingGenerator; assignment + placement solver.
@plat/hood (stage 2, built after the base): RingFabric / SquareFabric / StreetFabric and the neighbourhood LOD workflow; the interface lives in @plat/layout.

@plat/labels: S13a names (every node of the quarter tree), candidates and spines; S13b view placement over parameters the renderer passes in (ObstacleSource, RoleIndex) — never imports render; font-metrics reader; collision; furniture incl. the ruler and the emblem generator.

@plat/render: S14 columnar display-list builder, paint programs, style sheets, LOD, tile pyramid and tile worker (which runs S13b by calling @plat/labels), backends (Canvas2D, SVG, print tiles; WebGL2 tile compositor as fallback), shadow pass, decoration stamps over the bundled stamp-tile asset (§8.10), live layers, the tile worker queue of resumable raster jobs (§8.9).
@plat/edit: edit events, dry-run validation, undo and redo records, scoped regeneration, rebase, dependency audit, event migrations, warp kernels.
@plat/export: geojson, svg, png/tiles (streaming), vtt (Foundry-class scene JSON, dd2vtt), gltf/obj, cityjson, csv, permalinks.
notes: §0.6 says CityJSON was added "to the deferrals" while §14 lists a cityjson exporter in the base (see the staged-list check).

statement: @plat/sim (optional, M4b): relation store materialised, postings, occupancy and schedules, calendar, factions, events, economy, personality and the stat-block pack (D-32), over @plat/content ids.
@plat/api: the handle-based facade (§11.2), generation worker host, derivation pool, host bridge (§11.3) and DocResolver (§11.5), the headless CLI.

@plat/docs: the user guide (generated reference pages from control, entity and table registries plus written pages); known-defects.json; release notes generated from plat/goldens/shifts/ and the milestone records (§13.3), the D-5 statuses (§13.6) and the known defects.
notes: §13.3 says the release-notes generator reads only the golden record files and known-defects.json; the D-5 status is carried in MilestoneRecord.d5, so not a conflict (VS5-3 names record.json as read by the release notes).

statement: @plat/testkit: B-FUZZ generators (random and constructive), invariant runners, cost-model tests, bench statistics and the parity CLI (reads baselines/baselines.json only), golden tooling with shift, cascade and milestone records and placement digests over plat/goldens/ (§13.3) and the one WaterSetting type, the O9 (c) faithfulness campaign (§13.2), the boolean and buffer oracles (Clipper2-WASM in Node, polygon-clipping), the clean-room scanner (§17), the D-5 seed list by H32 and the export command (plat d5 seeds, PNGs for §13.6), which read only the committed ftg-captures.json and ng-counts.json (§13.6 (2)).

Stage registrations with changed declared I/O (definitions in §4.1–§4.12): S3 outputs gate routes, travel-cost field T, stage-1 trace and gates, carved water with decks and decoration ponds, map border (L1), harbour route (after its L0 batch), forced harbour pick (§4.2 S3 (4)) and the §4.2 S3 (7) harbour gate where placed; S1 declares the arena outer ring (L0) and every crossing site as a Bridge in state site, built by S4/S5; S6 the settlement perimeter and Seam records (SeamEdge.type includes reserve with its reservation id); S7b passes claimSubFace a face list (within: FaceRef | FaceId[], §3.4); the castle template row carries townSide: dry_ditch | none (§4.8); S12a no geometry (sites only); the hinterland unit registers as a unit of S10/S10b/S11/S12b over the hinterland blocks (§4.9); SkyStrategy.place takes S7b sky allocations (II.6); BuildingInput.fixedWings, BaseWing.kind, BaseWing.corners and carryWings are §2.6s; SlotPlan §2.5s; SettingPack.rosterPatch §10.4s.
notes: Pure restatement with round narration in its heading; replace by pointers.

statement: Dependency order (lint-enforced): kernel ← model ← tables ← {site, content} ← layout ← plots ← labels ← render ← edit ← export ← api ← app; labels ← render (N-22): render tile worker runs S13b from labels, and drawn symbol extents and the display-list index reach it only as the parameters ObstacleSource and RoleIndex (declared by labels, implemented by render), so labels never imports render; shared types LodBand, Role, ZoomStop, LabelEntity come from model.
notes: NR5-2 adds LabelRows to the shared types from model.

statement: Further dependency rules: docs reads only the registries of model and tables; hood depends on layout/plots only through their interfaces; sim depends on content and model only; render never imports layout; nothing depends on app; no package imports a backend it does not need; every adopted runtime library is imported in exactly one adapter file of the one package using it.

Model packages obey the §6.5 allowlist lint, which also scans vendored dependency sources; so do @plat/labels and the renderer code feeding S13b (every ObstacleSource and RoleIndex implementation, the functions they call, and the S14 builder code writing the columns they read — bbox, geometry ranges and GeomTable, layer, z, symbol extents from style-sheet sizes); CI finds that code as the TypeScript import closure of those implementations and column writers, so a joining module is linted without being listed; the rest of @plat/render stays outside the lint (§6.5 (3), §13.3).
notes: Stated three times in this part (§13.3, §14 rules, §14 comment). VS2-4 citation is history.

statement: No import, fixture or script path may resolve outside plat/ (§17).

Stage<I, O> extends StageDecl (§4.12): version; lineageUnit: EntityKind (§6.3); workLimits: WorkLimits (laws over the batch scope population-derived counts, §5.1 (5); coefficients in workLimits.json); budgetMs: Record<Rung, number> (reporting only); txForm: declared | callback (§3.3); inputsOf(model, scope): I; run(input, ctx): KernelResult<O>.
ConcernId = u16 branded number from the concern registry (§6.1), generated as typed constants, never a string.

StreamOpts {reroll (the derivation unit reroll, §6.1); attempt (ladder retry ≤ the concern registered cap: 3 for geometric ladders, 8 for naming, §6.1, §9.6); epoch; salt (the concern current salt from the recipe and the log rerollLayer events; 0 for geometry concerns)}.

StageContext {doc; plats: Record<PlatKey, Plat>; stream(concern, entity: Handle (entity key cached in the arena beside its lineage hash; TOWN_ROOT for town-level draws), opts): Stream; streamOpts(concern, entity, attempt?) (defaults: reroll from the entity derivation unit, epoch from context, salt from document); tables: TableView; rung: RungProfile (§1.1); report: ReportSink; scope?; epoch}.

TOWN_ROOT: the handle of the town itself as a derivation unit; its entity key is the seed key mixed with the fixed town lineage (ground arena, no parent, creation epoch 0, index 0), so town-level draws (S0 features, terrain noise, compass and emblem furniture §9.5) depend on the recipe alone, never on docId.
Scope = {kind: all} | {kind: entities, ids} | {kind: region, ring: Polygon, key: PlatKey, level} | {kind: epoch, epoch}; no raw face ids at the API.
StrategyRegistry: Maps for terrain, coast, river, manifest, network, enceinte, fabric, plots, sitePlan, building (BuildingGenerator), evolution, sky, sewer strategies.

FabricStrategy.partition(district, seam: SeamContract, ctx: DistrictContext, sc, k) → KernelResult<{blocks, ways}>; PlotStrategy.subdivide(block, ctx: BlockContext, claims, sc, k) → {plots, alleys, residue}; SitePlanStrategy.plan(plot, ctx: ContextVector, tables, rng, k) → SitePlan; GranularityLaw.bands(ctx, rung) → {frontageM, depthM, areaM2 ranges, joinMax, vacancyRunShare} (the deep-interior choice is S8s, §4.6).

Kernel facade: plat(key); view(key, level): LevelView; resolve(ref: GeomRef, key); geom: GeomOps; index: SpatialIndex; tx<T>(tx: KernelTx, fn?) with exactly one form (tx.ops declared, or fn callback, §3.3); KernelTx carries stage and rederivesFrom; resolveVertexAt, signature and sampleProfile are §3.4 services.

Rng.stream(entityKey: Hash128, stage: u16 (STAGE_VIEW = 0xffff for paint programs and furniture), concern: ConcernId, opts: StreamOpts): Stream; StageContext.stream is rng.stream with the calling stage id and the entity cached key; no string reaches the mixer (the textual key form of §6.1 is for reports only); a lint rejects a stream call whose concern is not a ConcernId.

ContentProvider (a host own roster or people; registered only after the §11.4 double-run check, outputs recorded in the document): id; version; roster(pop, character: CharacterVector, tables, rng): Roster; site(roster, plots, ctx: SitingContext, rng): SitingResult; people(household, rng): Person[].

ObstacleSource (declared by labels, implemented by render): protectedExtents(stop, box) → {box, entity, kind: gate | castle | plaza | bridge | wall}[] (drawn symbol extents, §9.2); coverage(stop, box) → {labels, protected, buildings, ways, water} (mark cover for furniture, §9.5). RoleIndex: roleAt(p, band): Role (area mark under a point, halos §9.4); snap(p, radiusPx, stop): Point | null (measure tool §9.5). Both implemented by render over a display list: in the tile worker for S13b, furniture and ruler (main thread via §8.9 queries), in the generation worker over an SVG export transient list, and in the tile worker over a raster export list (§11.1); every implementation under the §6.5 lint.

LabelPlacer: begin(stop, labels: LabelEntity[], obstacles, roles, fonts: FontMetrics, memo: PlacementMemo): PlacementJob; place(same args): PlacementSet (= begin then step(Infinity)); view data (§9.2). PlacementJob: step(deadlineMs): boolean (runs units from where it stopped, returns after the first unit ending ≥ deadlineMs after the call began; true when complete); result(); cancel(); readonly spentMs — resumable so the tile worker serves queries between units (§8.9, §9.2).
notes: Open item NR5-2: begin and place take a LabelRows view (declared in @plat/model) instead of LabelEntity[]. NR4-2 citation is history.

statement: Pointers: @plat/model — LabelEntity, QuarterNode (§9.1), LodBand, Role, ZoomStop (§8.1, §8.2, §8.8); @plat/render — DisplayList, MarkTable, DisplayDelta, DisplayListBuilder (§8.1), StyleSheet, Symbolisation, OrderSlot, LiveLayerProvider (§8.2), LayerSpec (§8.4), backends and threads (§8.9); @plat/api — PlatApi, DocHandle (§11.2), BridgeTransport, BridgeMessage (§11.3), DocResolver (§11.5); @plat/testkit — Baseline, ParityReport (§13.5), ShiftRecord, CascadeRecord, MilestoneRecord, WaterSetting (§13.3), D5Record, D5Pair, H32 (§13.6), CorpusAdapter, CalibrationRun (§13.9).

TileAddress {stop, i, j, dpr}; TileRasterOpts {layers, tileLayer: base | under | shadow | over, shadows: off | drop | prism (§8.2 StyleSheet.shadows.projected), sun?: {azimuthCdeg, altitudeCdeg}, tier: low | mid | high, dpr}; TileBackend.begin(tile, list, style, opts): RasterJob (fixes the tile draw sequence, draws nothing, §8.9).
notes: Open item NR5-1: add lightStep?: {azimuthCdeg, altitudeCdeg} beside sun? (read by faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade, crowns; sun? read only by the projected-shadow pass).

statement: RasterJob: step(deadlineMs): boolean (runs on from where it stopped; returns after the first draw call ending ≥ deadlineMs after the call began; true when complete); finish(): ImageBitmap; cancel(); readonly spentMs — resumable (§8.9). VectorBackend.write(list, style, {layers, band, frame}): string.

EditEngine: apply(doc, e): ApplyResult (Ok | Conflict(actions) | Confirm(token, fates, renames); an event carrying fates and renames commits only when a fresh dry run computes the same, §11.2); undo(doc, session, of?) (appends an undo event, §7.4; of only for the owner role); redo(doc, session); replay(base, log, {toSeq?, mode: interactive | replay}): Model; migrate(doc, to): {doc, diff}; rebase(doc, reason, at?) — at defaults to the log head; the only other allowed value is h0 (the decoded snapshot model.seq, when the saved town is kept after edits made during load verification, §2.9 step 4, §7.1); any other at returns {status: conflict, actions: [{kind: invalid, message: E_REBASE_AT: at must be the log head or h0}]}, appends and rebases nothing, on every host alike.
notes: VD4-4, VD3-7, VS4-2 citations are history.

statement: Exporter<Opts> {id; write(doc, list: DisplayList | null, opts): Promise<Uint8Array | string>} — runs in the generation worker (§11.1); list = the transient export list for SVG and raster formats (a raster format transfers it to the tile worker with its raster-export request, §8.9, §11.1); null for model formats (GeoJSON, glTF/OBJ, CityJSON, CSV, the document forms).

@plat/app, the reference UI: one click; the basic panel (≤ 12 controls, §7.8) and the advanced panel; report panel; editing tools (draw, move, warp, brushes, the four actions, lock, assign); tables editor and style dialog; ruler (§9.5); gazetteer and "features in view" list; context help; family-tree view (module).

Input scheme (COV-MFCG-L08), MFCG idiom, held in keymap.json (data, editable, versioned): click selects and opens the context panel; double-click zooms to the entity band (district fills the view); shift+click = New random on the entity scope keeping its kind; ctrl/cmd+click resets the entity to generated (one logged event applying the inverses of its own edits); alt+click toggles lock; right-click/long-press opens context actions (§7.4); dragging a selected vertex = moveVertex; wheel/pinch zooms; drag empty map pans. Keys with map focus: A alleys at city band, B buildings, D grid, N hairline mode, L labels, T trees, M ruler, W warp tool (then 1–8 kernel), G gazetteer, F features in view, R New random on selection, Esc cancel, ctrl/cmd+Z undo, ctrl/cmd+shift+Z redo, + / − zoom, 0 fit, ? keymap overlay; bindings active only while the map region has focus; a host can switch global bindings off; every bound action also on a menu or button.

Accessibility (COV-FTG-A24): the app chrome meets WCAG 2.2 level AA; landmarks header (title and seed), navigation (panels), main (map region role=application with accessible name and live description — rung, band, district under pointer or focused entity), complementary (report, gazetteer); accessible names/descriptions from the control registry; every icon button has a text label; keyboard focus order follows layout, visible focus, no trap; map takes arrow-key panning and + / − zoom; the non-visual route is the gazetteer (list and search via query) and the "features in view" list (visible entities grouped by kind, ordered by distance from view centre, announcing name, kind, district), selection synced both ways; UI text contrast ≥ 4.5 : 1, UI components ≥ 3 : 1 (map follows the §8.2 contrast matrix); reduced-motion turns off animated zoom; UI scales 100–200 %; tests §13.4.

Context help and guide (COV-FTG-A25): every control and panel links to its anchor in @plat/docs (§7.8), opened in a side panel; reference pages generated from the control registry (label, range, unit, output metric, consuming stage, locality class), entity registry and table schemas (columns, units, provenance); written pages cover getting started, each panel, each edit action, each export and the tables editor; release notes generated per release from the shift records (§13.3) and known-defects.json (id, symptom, affected rungs and presets, workaround, since, fixed-in); tests §13.2.
values: known-defects fields: id, symptom, rungs/presets, workaround, since, fixed-in

statement: Family-tree view (COV-FTG-C11; module tier, M4b): reads query(h, {kind: relations, person, up: n, down: m}) over the relation store (§10.3); generations in rows by birth epoch, partners side by side, children below; branches beyond two generations elided into an expandable count; re-root on any person; opening a person never pins it (§10.3); keyboard-operable as a tree grid.

Extension points: every Map in StrategyRegistry (stage 2 registers three template fabrics; a village registers a tracker NetworkStrategy, palisade EnceinteStrategy, density StageDecl and houses-along-ways FabricStrategy; owner-staged layers register SkyStrategy and SewerStrategy; the evolution engine an EvolutionStrategy); BuildingGenerator (stage 3); StageDecl registration by declared IO; PaintProgram, StyleSheet and LiveLayerProvider registries; Exporters; rule tables, presets, rung profiles, setting packs and keymaps (data); EditEvent kinds with migrations; LayerSpecs; ContentProvider (after the double-run check); BridgeTransport and DocResolver; the PlacementSolver; CorpusAdapter (§13.9).

Two checklists: the parity matrix (every capability recorded in the four references and where it lives — MFCG and FTG rows in the base, NG rows in the stage-2 interface, VG rows checked only as not blocked) and the improvement matrix (every committed improvement, its mechanism, the number that proves it and the kind of proof).

Parity tags: BASE (delivered by stage 1), STAGE-2 (delivered by the neighbourhood stage through an interface the base carries), VILLAGE-LATER (separate product staged by the owner; checked as not precluded, hooks in PART III), module (optional @plat/sim, M4b), hook; "beyond" marks rows where the base deliberately exceeds the reference weakness; rows with ids starting a: come from the coverage audits (COV-FTG-OBS1) so the matrix is no coarser than the findings.
notes: "added by the fix-all pass" is history.

statement: MFCG has 40 rows, all BASE. A1 parameter surface/blueprint/URL → §4.2 S0, §6.4 permalinks, §7.7 intent (flags as intent toggles and the features strip §7.8); A2 RNG stream/seed chain/save-restore → §6.1 keyed sub-streams (beyond); A3 pipeline and failure policy → §4.1, §5 (beyond: no whole-city restart, every requested feature counted by delivery tier).

MFCG B1–B10: B1 patch mesh → replaced by the plat and backbone faces (§2.2, §4.3), Delaunator kept for site sampling, denser regular centre by stage regimes; B2 junction optimisation → §3.6 attraction + §4.3 junction merge (8 m), Y → T; B3 coast/sea → §4.2 S1 closed-outline coast at the request bearing; B4 buildDomains → §4.2 S1 flood fill of L0; B5 curtain wall/gates/towers/watergate → §4.2 S3 gate sites, §4.4 trace before the stage growth, §4.8 gates at arterials with exact N, water gates, towers by rule; B6 citadel/castle → §4.2 S3 reservation by score (inside / on-enceinte / outside), §4.8 keep by lir, bailey, 0.75 compactness gate as a shape check repaired in MFCG order (angle equalisation, then bloat within the area band), then re-sited, then a keep without a bailey, never a restart (F-CASTLE); B7 streets and roads → §4.3 routed arterials to gates/market/bridges/harbour; B8 rivers/canals → §4.2 S1 rivers by descent, distributaries, estuary as width rule, islands, §4.8 bridges, canals as an intent flag; B9 districts → §4.5 grower over coarse faces, check4holes, feature-named kinds, quarters; B10 ward → blocks → §4.6 bent-cut infill (intramural secondaries and lanes as spines).

MFCG B11–B20: B11 block → lots → §4.7 S10 per-frontage plots + front jitter (ruling O5; statistics matched §13.5); B12 outskirts falloff → §4.4 ribbon regime with distance-to-gate kernel, §4.5 density field; B13 shanty/ribbon → §4.5 squalid type after the first half of the stages outside the enceinte with MFCG trigger set, §4.4 ribbon regime, suburb regime on the shanty toggle; B14 plaza/temple/churches/gate plazas → §4.2 S3 plaza sized per rung, §4.7 S9 square faces, §4.8 gate plazas and church forecourts (G-R1), institutions via claims; B15 landmarks/keep → §4.7 S11 institution site plans, §2.6 landmark footprint templates and OutlineBuildingGenerator, lir keep, solid-ink landmarks in ink (BASE + stage-3 hook); B16 greens/parks → §4.9 greenery table; B17 farms/fields → §4.9 hinterland presets incl. furrow style; B18 harbour → §4.8 water furniture (basin, moles, quays, piers at 12–20 m); B19 trees/forests → §4.9 forests as faces, §8.10 stamped ranked tiles (Poisson k = 50, built at product build and shipped, four seam-compatible variants sharing one border band, scaled per entity by spacing); B20 elevation → §4.2 S1 real heightfield feeding S4/S5 costs (beyond).

MFCG C1–C3, D1–D3: C1 display modes → §8.5 LOD bands + plot model (Lots look = footprint masses over ground at city band; Hidden = layer toggle; optional cadastral layer; beyond: no global switch); C2 roofs Plain/Hip/Gable, Raised, Solids → §3.8 skeleton with plain-roof downgrade, §8.2 roof program, §2.6 roof spec and heights, Raised = ink offset under-copy on by default (projected shadow off, §8.4); C3 lot Offset → §4.7 S11 front-line jitter; D1 naming → §10.4 own engine and grammar; D2 district labels → §9 hole-aware spines, quarter labels at city zoom, OBB-arc / straight / legend fallbacks (beyond: protected features); D3 furniture → §9.5 (emblem slot with import and a minimal own generator; compass reroll).

MFCG E1–E4, F1–F3, G1–G2, H1–H2: E1 colour system → §8.2 roles, contrast matrix, per-entity tints, thematic overrides; E2 strokes/order/caching → §8.2–§8.3 (casing idiom, round joins, order parity, world-aligned tiles); E3 alleys → §4.6 lanes/alleys are ways, §8.5 access-critical lanes at the city band; E4 district view/framing/no-zoom/thin lines → §8.8 continuous zoom on 2^¼ stops + district band, framing §9.5, hairline mode (key N); F1 warp tools (8) → §3.4 warp + §7.1 warp event with dry run and whole-step validation; F2 rerolls/renames/landmarks → §7.1 named actions, setAttr, assign (beyond: persisted, undoable); F3 UI/hotkeys/size bands → @plat/app keymap.json (§14), measure tool (§9.5), size ladder as data (§1.1); G1 export PNG/SVG/JSON → §11 (beyond: round-trip import, layered SVG); G2 integrations → §11 API, host bridge, static exports; emblem our own (§9.5); no third-party service (BASE hook); H1 population and scale → §10.2 population as input, §2.1 metres; H2 performance → §12 (matched sizes 40/80/130; §12.9 declared trade).

FTG has 46 rows + 9 audit rows, BASE unless noted. A1 parameters/presets/save → §4.2 S0, §7.6 presets as data, §2.9 document; A2 two-phase pipeline/failure → §4.1 (programme before layout, two-way), §5; A3 coordinates/units/wire → §2.1 integer cm centred, §2.9 binary blocks/CBOR twin; A4 determinism and old settlements → §6, §6.4 retention, §7.5 migrate (beyond); A5 server/client, persistence, lazy people → §11.2 handle API and workers, §2.9, §10.3; a:A24 accessibility and list/search views → §14 @plat/app accessibility, gazetteer and features-in-view, §13.4 tests; a:A25 guide, context help, release notes naming defects → §14 @plat/docs, §7.8 anchors, §13.2 checks.

FTG B rows: B1 size ladder/population/area → §1.1 ladder and rung profiles, §4.2 S2 stage quotas, §12.2; B2 dependency-graph selection → §10.2 sequential roster (own tables); B3 residents/postings/backfill/matching → §10.3 households (base), postings and re-matching in the module (BASE + module); B4 people → §10.3 derived people with ancestry rows (BASE + module data depth); B5 government/religion/factions/military → §2.7 Faction/Institution with seats, §10.2 government and religion rows, meetings/roles/goals in the module (BASE + module); B6 relations/events → relation-store schema in base (§10.1), materialised by @plat/sim (module); a:B10 economy → D-32 @plat/sim over the base schema stub (§10.3), roster provides/uses edges (§10.2) (module); a:C03 personality/education/stat block → D-32 @plat/sim from the person key, stat block a named game-system pack off by default (module); a:C11 family-tree view → §14 (module).

FTG C1–C10: C1 coast/islands/ponds → §4.2 S1 closed-outline routine, bank classes (also sky islands); C2 rivers → §4.2 S1 hydrology, tributaries, distributaries, river islands, crossing sites, §4.8 bridges; C3 drawn water → §7.1 drawWater; C4 road-graph substrate → §2.2 the plat (beyond: attraction, levels as views, role sets on edges); C5 road growth → §4.4 S5 outside the walls (mean-reverting curvature walk, destination-biased, explicit legality; per-preset rules for american/ringed), travel-cost stage boundaries with the anisotropy row; C6 district lots → §4.5 grower and typing, merge floor, S7b allocation; C7 district internal pipeline → §4.7 claims → S8 → S10 → S11, Dense/Gaps/Individually ≈ row/detached/compound, tents row (§4.7 S11), building-scale multiplier (§2.5); C8 lot → plot → §4.7 S10 per-frontage regions (ruling O5); C9 footprints/landmarks/entrances → §4.7 S11, entrance rule, non-rectangular landmark templates (§2.6); C10 suburb stage → §4.4 suburb regime (offshoots, cul-de-sacs, small lots, density Bernoulli) by preset or shanty toggle.

FTG C11–C18 and audits: C11 walls/towers → §4.8; C12 castle district → §4.2 S3 + §4.8; C13 harbours/waterfront → §4.8 water furniture, §4.5 docks; C14 outer settlement → §4.9 S12a count-driven outside land, farmsteads, outside buildings on resources (§10.2 outside rows); C15 forests/trees/hedgerows → §4.9, §8.2 hedgerow instances in lit; a:I11 tree species → §2.7 Greenery.species from the climate table, §4.9 inner/outer shares; C16 decorations/reserve/climate → ponds carved at S3 (§4.2 S3 (10)), rest of decoration table (copses, stone circles, ruins with trails, counts by rung and biome, keep-clear radii) as S12a sites built by the hinterland unit (§4.9), reserve land use, climate as circumstance + style preset (BASE should-have); a:I05 feathered field edges → §8.2 feather program on in lit; C17 perimeter expand/round and decorations → §4.5 S6 settlement perimeter offset and rounded, §4.7 furniture pins, plot boundary treatments (§2.5); a:J05 market stalls → §4.7 furniture pins on the square edge band and round the market hall; C18 naming/erosion → §10.4 (contraction as an EVO event).

FTG D–H rows: D1 renderer → §8.1 columnar display list + tile backends (hit-test slices); D2 palette → §8.2 lit preset on Canvas2D with our texture set; D3 roofs → §3.8, §8.2 (cached per entity revision); D4 water/coast decoration → §8.2 bands, depth ramp, foam, bank classes; D5 day/night/weather/seasons/window lights → §8.4 sun vector + shadow hook, night preset with lights role, lights from the module (BASE hook + module); D6 post effects → §8.2 per-tile post operations (greyscale, sepia, tint, vignette, pixelate, dot screen, scanline, crosshatch noise) (should-have); D7 labels/scale/grid/units/legend/thematic → §9, thematic layers = style overrides keyed by attributes (§8.2); a:L08 ruler → §9.5 measure tool (distance and area, metres and feet, snapping); D8 3-D/street view/height maps → §11 glTF and CityJSON exports, heights in the model, no 3-D default view (R13) (BASE export); E1 layout editor → §7.1 draw/move/warp with split-on-cross and dry run; E2 regenerate area/bulk/constrained reroll → §7.1 named actions, setAttr batches, faithful regeneration (beyond: undoable); E3 entity editing/dictionaries/pins/notes/layers → §7.1 setAttr, data dictionaries by id (§10.3), annotation layer (§9.5), view notes (§11.3), LayerSpec; F1 schedules/behaviours/sub-locations → §10.3 module, sub-locations with capacities (§2.6); F2 clock/calendar/time sync → §10.3 module, time view state and module command over the bridge (§11.3); G1 export → §11 (beyond: districts in GeoJSON, per-layer VTT, CityJSON); G2 integrations → §11 VTT exports (Foundry-class, dd2vtt) + host bridge, no hosted service (§11.5); H1 data scale → §12.8, lazy people.

FTG H2 performance → §12 (beyond: client-side): first map under 1 s for every TOWN and CITY and METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings (≈ 48 000 people), ≈ 2.3 s at the 120 000 cap; model p95 within O3 (d) bars up to ≈ 4 500 / 17 700 / 58 800 people and max up to ≈ 3 400 / 13 600 / 45 800; both misses declared for veto (D-18, §12.3, §12.5).
