statement: Clean-room posture in brief: never copy or port reference code (the 2017 ancestor is GPL, live builds proprietary); re-implement published ideas and measured behaviour; reference name lists, palettes, building tables and textures are never reused, ours are written fresh; product writers read only this document and a cleaned digest; the product folder cannot reach research folders; reference numbers reach tests through one numbers-only file; a scanner stops the build on a reference word list, palette or table; every library permissive, pinned and credited in a generated notices file so the owner can choose any licence.

Who reads what: research seats (readers, measurers, the digest writer) may read findings, captures/, research/ and — under the standing ruling — reference/; implementer seats (anyone writing code, tables, style sheets, content, assets or tests in plat/) read only docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, the implementer digest in plat/docs/digest/, the plat/ repository, published algorithm papers and adopted libraries' public documentation; they never open research/, captures/, reference/, the findings, the critics, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md, docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md or red-team files; citations are for traceability and an implementer follows them only into the digest; no code from TownGeneratorOS (GPL-3), the FTG Foundry module or any captured bundle is read for implementation, ported or paraphrased.

The implementer digest: a digest seat writes plat/docs/digest/ from the research — behaviours, measured numbers (each with its baselines.json id or finding reference) and the creators' stated ideas; no code excerpts, reference word lists, grammars, palettes, tables or identifiers; a separate checker seat reading only the digest runs the content scan on it and files a report; every digest change repeats the check; this document is held to the same rule (FTG-22).

Until M-1 builds the deny-list, every seat that writes this document (a fix-all integration seat, an amendment pass's apply and repair lanes, any finishing or repair seat) runs before its change lands: python3 docs/validation/bench/doc_checks.py --sections "⟨every section heading key the change touched⟩" from the project root — content checks (iii) and (vi) over the touched sections, the others over the whole document.
notes: This pass writes docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, so the Assemble seat is bound by it.

statement: doc_checks (i) identifiers: whole-word, case-sensitive search for the backticked identifiers of research/findings/ftg-payload-visual.md §7.2 plus one further time-setting message name — 36 names read from the finding or held research-side, none copied into this document.

doc_checks (ii) colours: every six-digit colour value (#rrggbb or 0xrrggbb) looked up case-insensitive and hex-delimited in research/ (text files incl. JSON), captures/**/README*.md, captures/**/*.json, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md and docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md.

doc_checks (iii) token 3-grams: lower-cased word tokens of the changed sections against every 3-gram of research/findings/*.md and of the string keys and values of every JSON file under research/ and captures/, in document order with numeric tokens dropped; a hit is a run of three or more consecutive shared 3-grams (five or more tokens in a row standing together in a source); a single shared 3-gram is ordinary phrasing.

doc_checks (iv) tables: outside fenced code (fences may be indented) every line starting with | ends with |, no other line sits between two table lines, and every row has its header's number of cells counting only unescaped pipes; inside a table a pipe in code is written \| (GFM splits cells at every unescaped pipe, even in a code span).
doc_checks (v) pointers: every §n and §n.m pointer resolves to a heading of this document.
notes: The consolidation must keep every pointer resolvable after moving text (e.g., Judgment calls to the rationale file).

statement: doc_checks (vi) lists in any order: every JSON file under research/ and captures/ except the profiler's recordings (call censuses, coverage, idle, trace, draw and path records, run reports, metadata, session and index files) is read for its lists (a dict's keys, an array of strings, one field's string values across ≥ 3 records); a hit is a line of the changed sections holding ≥ 5 distinct whole words of ≥ 4 letters that are members of one such list, reported sorted.

Each hit is corrected before the change lands or reviewed into docs/validation/doc-checks-allow.tsv with its check, exact text and a written reason (capture-citation file name, measured number, creator sentence under 15 words quoted for traceability, ordinary phrasing, generic vocabulary in our own selection and order, pointer into another document); the script exits non-zero while any hit is unreviewed; the change does not land until it exits zero; the seat records its counts in its output file (fix-all integration log; amendment pass in docs/validation/amendments-applied.md and amendments-repair.md); from M-1 the hashed scan of (5) also runs over this document and replaces (i)–(iii) and (vi), while (iv) and (v) stay.

Calibration (executed): on §13–§17 after round 2 (pre-round-3 lines 6657–7826, md5 ca2e2066…, docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r4_calib_pre_r3_s13_s17.txt), 1 196 of 26 236 token 3-grams shared with the findings forming 47 runs of ≥ 5 tokens (45 distinct: §13 24, §14 4, §15 11, §16 6, §17 2); no run threshold 1–7 gives the 27 an earlier draft stated; on the round-3 text the same rule gives 53 runs; (ii) finds none of the document's 36 colour values in its sources; (iv) found exactly the one broken row VS2-1 names, and the cell-count clause exactly one more (J-I15); the round-4 JSON extension over 2 052 JSON files (≈ 30–45 s) adds 50 distinct run texts to (iii) and (vi) flags 8 lines of generic vocabulary, all reviewed into the allow file; of 429 one-line lists in FTG's content database, (vi) catches all 429 in either order while (iii) catches none of the alphabetised five-name lines and 210 in database order.
notes: Executed-evidence narration; compress to a pointer.

statement: Chose scripted proxies with a reviewed allow file over a hand-run grep (the round-2 hand proxy checked identifiers only and passed any pasted palette or table); chose to bind every seat that writes this document over the integration seat alone (amendment lanes write it directly; J-S32); chose the list check (vi) beside the extended 3-gram check because a reordered list shares no 3-gram with its source (J-S35).
notes: Inline rationale duplicated with the Judgment calls rows.

statement: Repository boundary: the product is its own repository plat/ at the folder root outside research/, captures/ and reference/; a PR-tier CI rule fails any import specifier, fixture path, script path or build input resolving outside plat/ (symbolic links resolved); the product's CI never reads the research trees.

Reference numbers only through committed numbers-only files: research-side scripts (research/baselines/) measure the captures and write Baseline rows with provenance into baselines.json, committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/; the parity CLI reads only it; the D-5 panel is assembled research-side from product PNG exports and capture images, and "its only inputs to the product are two numbers-only files" in plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/ — ftg-captures.json (capture ids, rungs, water settings, resident counts) and ng-counts.json (NG building counts) — which plat d5 seeds reads.
notes: Conflict SCOPE-C02 (open item VS5-3): §13.6 (9) commits a third product file, record.json.

statement: Content scan: research/baselines/make_denylist.py builds the deny-list from the creative data the findings and captures record (naming-grammar rule names and terminal words, Markov and corpus sample words, palette colours, FTG building-type, profession, item and service identifiers and names, FTG Foundry-module message and field names, texture and image file hashes); the list holds only salted SHA-256 digests — of single normalised tokens (lower-cased, diacritics stripped) not in §9.6's spell-check list, of token 3-grams in list order, of exact six-digit colours, of file bytes, and per recorded list the set of salted digests of its members' words of ≥ 4 letters.

@plat/testkit's clean-room scanner digests the same way every token of @plat/tables, assets, source string literals and comments and the digest in the PR tier; it flags as a list hit any line or table column holding ≥ 5 distinct words of one list's set; a hit fails the build unless a reviewed allow entry with a written reason is added (an authored roster sharing ordinary building or trade names is such an entry; the review decides whether the selection was copied).

At every milestone the checker seat runs a research-side palette audit: a shipped palette with three or more colours within ΔE2000 2 of one reference palette fails and is redesigned; every file in plat/assets names the script that generated it or its third-party licence (fonts); a file with neither fails the build.

Honest provenance: every table cell's provenance is one of own, ref:⟨reference⟩ ⟨behaviour⟩ (a measured or stated behaviour admissible as a calibration anchor — e.g. MFCG castle 0.75 compactness gate, FTG 40 m bridge spacing and 39 m tower spacing, NG's lane-width law, Poisson k = 50), owner, owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩, architecture ⟨date⟩, corpus or host; a number describing a behaviour is a fact; a list, grammar, palette or table is creative content, never reused.

The record: plat/docs/CLEAN-ROOM.md holds the rule, the seat ledger (which seat read which research file, from the lane logs), the digest checker's reports and the deny-list's generation record (date, sources, counts — never the tokens).

Sources of algorithms (published; each read in its published form, the seat ledger records which): Shewchuk predicates; snap rounding (Hobby; Guibas–Marimont; Hershberger); winding-number arrangement booleans; Bridson Poisson-disc; Felkel–Obdržálek and Aichholzer straight skeletons; Chaikin; Visvalingam–Whyatt; Parish–Müller growth; Lloyd relaxation; marching squares; priority-flood; Garbrecht–Martz flat resolution; fBm with ridged multifractal and domain warping (Musgrave in Ebert et al. 2003); xoshiro128** with Irwin–Hall normals; MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit and its 32-bit finaliser (H128 §6.2, RH32 §8.1, H32 §13.6) checked against SMHasher values; Krüger transverse Mercator in Karney's formulation to fourth order (§11.1); van der Corput radical inverse and Morton interleaving (§8.10); Ulichney void-and-cluster (§8.10); monotone-chain hull and rotating calipers (§3.1); centripetal Catmull–Rom and pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing; Dijkstra and A*; Brandes betweenness; Kruskal; Lambert shading; CIELAB and CIEDE2000; D8 flow and accumulation (O'Callaghan and Mark 1984); exact EDT (Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher 2012); three-pass box Gaussian (Wells 1986); Merkle tree (1987; D-28); Tracery-style grammar and n-gram Markov (ideas only, own grammar and corpora); power diagrams with area targets (Aurenhammer et al.) for §4.9 hinterland lots; Kahn topological sort with stage-id tie-break (§4.1, §4.12); SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4); for tests: Pearson χ² with Holm, Spearman, Moran's I, KS, SSIM, pair-correlation (Stoyan and Stoyan 1994), Shannon entropy, Jaccard index, Hausdorff distance; the round-4 list was checked by a scripted scan of 119 method names.
notes: Round attributions ("with the round-2 and round-3 text", "with the round-4 text") are history.

statement: The creators' stated ideas admitted (with constants calibrated on our own measurements): twisted bisection, the casing idiom, skeleton labels, the proposal queue, dependency ratios, lazy people, integer centimetres.

Protocol names (FTG-22): the host bridge vocabulary is our own (§11.3) — concurrency token logHead (§2.9) carried as baseLogHead and currentLogHead; time is the view key time set by view.set; the simulation module advances it with sim.advance { hours } (§10.3, §11.3); schema-level ideas (event/command split, optimistic-concurrency token) are admissible; FTG module message, command and field names are not reused, are in the deny-list and occur nowhere in this document (check (i)).

Fonts are third-party OFL assets outside the clean-room rule; chose IM FELL Great Primer (OFL) as the default label face over a different serif chosen "for clean-room distance" because it is MFCG's label face and part of the ink look the owner adopted (D-1); EB Garamond and Cinzel ship as alternatives.

Fonts ship unmodified; CI reads each face's name table and refuses to subset a face declaring a Reserved Font Name; the OFL text ships in the notices file; label metrics are read from the bundled files (§9.2); bundled faces are TrueType-flavoured (glyf) as SVG's default text writes (§11.1); when the default face lacks smcp the family's OFL small-caps cut is bundled unmodified beside it (§9.2); an SVG export may embed a face unmodified as a data URI (§11.1); CI checks all three (§9.2).

Our own licence (D-22): until the owner chooses, plat/ is proprietary — "Copyright © the owner. All rights reserved." in its LICENSE file, no open-source licence; chosen over an open licence because it keeps every option (publishing later under any licence is one act; an open licence once granted cannot be withdrawn); flagged for the owner's veto.
notes: Owner-rule tension (not an internal conflict): docs/OWNER-INSTRUCTIONS-2026-09-25.md records the owner's stated intent to license this module GPL-3; the document never mentions it. Not changed by this pass; reported for the owner/Fable.

statement: What keeps every licence choice open: permissive-only dependencies checked over the production closure (§17.4); nothing copyleft linked or bundled; the notices file; the clean-room chain (§17.1); every file written by the program's seats for the owner; no outside contribution without the owner's written assent.

Licence checker: the allowlist — MIT, ISC, BSD-2/3, Apache-2.0, BSL-1.0, CC0, Unlicense, OFL (fonts) and Sun's fdlibm notice — runs in the PR tier over the transitive production closure of every shipped bundle (library, embed, app, CLI); dev-only exceptions each with a reason: @resvg/resvg-js (MPL-2.0), Playwright and its browsers (MPL/LGPL components), axe-core (MPL-2.0), the oracles, the validators and the spell-check dictionary; Inkscape and QGIS are GPL programs CI runs as external tools and never links.

Notices: CI generates THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt from the production closure (name, version, licence text, copyright lines) plus the fonts' OFL text and the fdlibm notice; every bundle ships it; the minifier keeps /*! */ banners.

Pins: exact versions in every package.json with the lockfile committed; no prerelease in the production closure; an upgrade is a reviewed change re-running the checker, §6.5's allowlist scan of vendored sources and the goldens; every adopted runtime library is vendored at its pinned version into plat/vendor/, scanned by the determinism allowlist (§6.5), with an audit record kept in @plat/kernel.

Dependency table: robust-predicates 3.0.3 (Unlicense; incircle and the adversarial orient2d test reference; adopt, pinned); booleans/buffers/bands on the arrangement (ours, §3.7, built); straight skeleton with validator (ours, §3.8, built); dmath (our port of fdlibm 5.3 from netlib with Sun's notice, no @stdlib closure; built); Clipper2 (clipper2-wasm 0.4.0, BSL-1.0; CI oracle; the pre-decided M0 fallback would ship it compiled to WASM as the single engine, §3.7; dev, shipped only if the fallback fires); polygon-clipping 0.15.7 (MIT; CI oracle; dev); delaunator, d3-delaunay (ISC; site sampling, medial axes; adopt); earcut (ISC; triangulation for fields, glTF and CityJSON meshes; adopt); flatbush, rbush (ISC, MIT; spatial indices; adopt); simplex-noise (MIT; noise base; adopt, determinism checked by vendored scan); d3-contour (ISC; marching squares for render-tile contours; adopt); cbor-x (MIT; compact twin; adopt); zod (MIT; schemas; adopt); @napi-rs/canvas 1.0.9 (MIT; Node CLI PNG; optional, CLI only); fast-check, vitest, Playwright, pixelmatch, ssim.js, Vite, esbuild, tsx, pnpm, TypeScript (MIT/Apache-2.0/ISC; dev); axe-core (MPL-2.0; dev, never shipped); @resvg/resvg-js (MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft; headless SVG rendering in CI; dev, never shipped); OFL fonts IM FELL Great Primer (default), EB Garamond, Cinzel (SIL OFL 1.1; style assets unmodified).
notes: Conflict SCOPE-C05: Clipper2 row states the M0 fallback; §1.7 says oracles only.

statement: Nothing GPL, AGPL or LGPL is linked or bundled; CGAL is excluded (its straight skeleton is GPL); Boost.Geometry is BSL-1.0 with no GPL parts and is not used.

Delegated decisions: the owner deferred all judgment; each decision is final unless vetoed; each row states the choice, plain rationale, the rejected alternative and the cost to reverse; D-1–D-7 are the owner's adopted defaults (amendment 7) tied to mechanisms; decisions marked owner veto touch a subject the owner keeps (a purchase, the licence, new capability) and take the most option-preserving default, flagged.
notes: Owner-veto rows: D-18, D-22, D-31, D-32.

statement: D-1: default look = clean ink (MFCG family) with IM FELL Great Primer as label face; second preset FTG-like lit on Canvas2D like every preset; hatched preset for the close-up; house style = our own third preset house, drafted as three candidate sheets at M3b and chosen by the owner on the §13.6 panel at M4; ink stays default unless the owner picks otherwise; with no pick by M4's exit candidate 1 ships as house (never the default) and the pick is offered again at every later panel. Rejected: lit default; a WebGL2 reference backend for lit. Cost to reverse: low (a style file).
notes: House-pick mechanics are stated in D-1, §13.6 (8) and §16 M4 — keep the mechanics in §13.6 (8) and point from D-1.

statement: D-2: era and region centre of gravity = high-to-late medieval Western Europe (12th–15th c.) as presets the corpus phase re-signs via §13.9; walled shares and stage rows per rung MFCG-calibrated (≈ 0.9 of buildings inside the outermost wall, §4.2 S2); FTG's lower walled share reachable as a preset. Rejected: a hard-coded culture; a 0.35–0.5 walled share (MFCG's shanty case). Cost: low (table rows).

D-3: realism in the base; fantasy only as named toggles, each off by default — floating islands and their conjured rivers (II.6), fantasy sewers (II.6), the game-system stat pack (D-32), the night preset's lights. Rejected: fantasy defaults. Cost: low.

D-4: browser-first embeddable TypeScript library with an app on top; permissive dependencies only (§17.4 checker over the production closure); one generation worker, a derivation pool and a tile worker behind a handle-based API (§11.2). Rejected: Rust/WASM core from day one; server-side generation. Cost: medium after M1 for the core language (a measured hot loop may get a byte-identical WebAssembly accelerator, §3.7; there is no WASM kernel); low for the worker model.

D-5: "mastered" = the owner's eye on side-by-sides against MFCG and FTG at town/city/metropolis through §13.6's written blind protocol (seeds fixed beforehand, matched sizes, three questions, a pass rule, a filed record) plus §13.5's parity numbers; an unrated panel lets the build continue with D-5 status provisional — not rated, and "at parity", "mastered" and the stage-2 gate are claimed only by a rated pass or recorded owner acceptance (§13.6 (7)). Rejected: numbers only; an eye with no protocol. Cost: none.
notes: The unrated-panel rule is stated in D-5, §13.6 (7), §16 intro and each gating exit cell.

statement: D-6: original English-fantasy naming; setting packs in §10.4's format, the base shipping one pack; further packs are data. Rejected: reuse of reference corpora. Cost: low.

D-7: improvement weighting — realism, editability, plot texture first; speed and export next; novelty last — and it orders the build: the editing core (M2a) before the second preset and the rest of parity (M2b). Rejected: speed first; editing after the lit look. Cost: none.

D-8: 3-D export = glTF 2.0 (OBJ secondary) and CityJSON 2.0 (CityJSON integer vertices with a transform carry the centimetre lattice losslessly, so the exporter is thin, §11.1). Rejected: CityJSON left for later. Cost: low.
notes: Conflicts with §0.6 history ("CityJSON to the deferrals") — see SCOPE-C10.

statement: D-9: "no restart path" is a design property; acceptance numbers are requested-feature delivery by ladder tier (tier-6 omission of a requested feature a failure, target 0; degraded ≤ 5 %) and p95 time per delivered town on MFCG's worst configurations (≤ 1.0 s vs MFCG 3.7–4.0 s). Rejected: "0 whole-map restarts" as the number; a p99-bounded restart tier. Cost: low.

D-10: simulation depth in the base = roster, context vector, allocation and placement, households and lazy people, with the relation store's schema in the base from M1; schedules, calendar, factions' meetings, events, economy and personality in the optional @plat/sim module at its own milestone M4b. Rejected: schedules and calendar in the first release; the module inside M4. Cost: low.

D-11: Poisson-disc k = 50, all candidates evaluated, builds the per-class ranked tiles once when the product is built (hash-checked shipped asset, scaled per entity by spacing); per-instance placement is the stamp (§8.10); a measurement (NN p1, pair-correlation) may relax it. Rejected: k = 30; per-entity Bridson sampling. Cost: trivial (a table value).

D-12: integer centimetres centred on (0, 0), +y north; range invariant 2²³ cm; six-fold headroom over the largest frame (METROPOLIS at the population cap and extreme aspect, §3.2 (1)). Rejected: millimetres; doubles. Cost: high after M1.

D-13: five refinement levels as views of one arena per layer (level-tagged edges, per-level face records), a separate arena per layer and per sky island, unions for multi-face entities. Rejected: one flat subdivision; five separate per-level DCELs (nesting cannot hold on the lattice, GEO-1). Cost: high after M1.

D-14: booleans, buffers and bands on the kernel's own arrangement — one engine on every host; Clipper2 and polygon-clipping as CI oracles only; the straight skeleton built in-house under §3.8's contract and validator; the M0 bars and pre-decided fallbacks in §3.7–§3.8 (Clipper2-WASM as the single engine; the downgrades as the default paths). Rejected: CGAL (GPL); a JS skeleton port; a runtime pure-JS boolean fallback (second engine, different digests). Cost: low (adapters).
notes: Part of conflict SCOPE-C05 (D-14 says both "oracles only" and "Clipper2-WASM as the single engine").

statement: D-15: xoshiro128** streams keyed from structured components (seed key, entity lineage, stage, concern, reroll, attempt, epoch, salt), lineage separate from the address id, concern ids append-only; Enter = a new document with seed (seed + 1) mod 2³². Rejected: one global stream; a counter-based RNG. Cost: high after M1.
notes: §1.4's determinism row lists six components (stage, lineage, concern, reroll, attempt, epoch); D-15 lists eight (adds seed key, salt) — a summary vs full list, not a value conflict.

statement: D-16: the fused layout = routed arterials between named destinations; reservations and gate sites at S3 and each enceinte traced before its stage's growth; inside walls district-scale secondaries plus NG's bent-cut infill; outside them FTG-shaped growth with explicit legality and stage regimes; districts grown over the coarse skeleton, feature-named, grouped into quarters; frontage-first plots with the granularity law. Rejected: the four rejected shapes of §1.4 and §4.4; FTG growth to block scale inside the walls. Cost: high (layout core) — hence M0 and M1's gate.

D-17: enceinte — gate sites picked and castle and plaza reserved at S3; stage 1's enceinte traced at S3 from the travel-cost boundary over solved gate routes, each later enceinte at S5a from its stage boundary, both pulled to defensible ground before that stage's streets grow; gates exactly at arterial crossings with exact N by the measured gate law; gate plazas; castle by score with inside / on-enceinte / outside option; open waterfront by default. Rejected: wall on cell edges; tower-per-vertex; walls traced after growth. Cost: low.

D-18 (owner veto on the misses above the knees): budgets per §12.3 as per-rung laws of building count — model p95 TOWN ≤ 20 ms + 60 µs × B, CITY ≤ 40 ms + 50 µs × B, METROPOLIS ≤ 100 ms + 52 µs × B (100 / 300 / 800 ms at the targets); O3 (d) bars hold for p95 up to ≈ 1 333 / 5 200 / 17 300 buildings (≈ 4 500 / 17 700 / 58 800 people) and with the 1.25 × max clause up to ≈ 1 000 / 4 000 / 13 460 buildings; above them a declared miss (p95 ≈ 196 ms, ≈ 481 ms at TOWN and CITY band tops, ≈ 1.92 s at the METROPOLIS cap); the derivation pool primary wherever it measures within its law + 10 %, faster than a single worker, identical digests, the single worker the fallback elsewhere (measured at M1 TOWN/CITY, M2b METROPOLIS); the max clause judged on outliers confirmed by solo re-timing; first map per §12.5 — TOWN ≤ 40 ms + 70 µs × B, CITY ≤ 60 ms + 60 µs × B, METROPOLIS ≤ 120 ms + 62 µs × B — under 1 s for every TOWN and CITY and METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings (≈ 48 000 people), ≈ 2.3 s at 120 000, a declared miss of O12 (g); a per-building cost ≈ 2 × MFCG at TOWN and CITY and ≈ 5 × at METROPOLIS declared as a trade (§12.9). Rejected: workers without a merge protocol; matching MFCG cost by dropping plot detail; a preview or coarser one-click path above the knee. Cost: low (numbers); ≈ 1 pw for a district-by-district city band above the knee; medium if M0 or M1 miss.
notes: Fifth and fullest copy of the budget laws in this part; the numbers belong to §12; D-18 should state the decision and the veto and point there. See SCOPE-C01.

statement: D-19: codename PLAT and @plat/*; terrain resolution 5 / 8 / 10 m; frame areas 4 / 25 / 64 km² with aspect 0.5–2 (square by default) + 30 % margin, side scaling with √(population ÷ target); min edge 25 cm with attraction at 26 cm; min plot width 2.5 m; min plot angle 12°; the district band derived from the count law; the gate law round(1 + 0.47 √A_ha); stage counts and walled shares per rung (§1.1, §4.2 S2); shadows off by default with a fixed sun; heights always populated; tower spacing and every band as calibratable table rows. Cost: trivial (data).
notes: See conflict SCOPE-C09 (PLAUSIBLE): min plot width 2.5 m vs §15.2 O5 (b) "0 plots < 3 m".

statement: D-20: effort ≈ 153–204 expert person-weeks — base 139–186 (content module included) plus stage 2 14–18, re-derived line by line in §16; the fix-all pass's mechanisms priced in their own line, rounds 4–5's six new components at 3–4 pw; the cuts reducing it to ≈ 136–176 recorded for the owner's veto, not applied. Rejected: 100–130 pw; cutting scope to hold it. Cost: none (an estimate).

D-21: the document persists a base (recipe or rebased state) and the ordered log, with a digest-verified snapshot cache; one replay fold; a rebase when a saved state is kept; output versions N−1 and N−2 retained in the browser and every version in the CLI; an upgrade is an undoable event. Rejected: events only; "last N minor versions replayable" with no mechanism. Cost: low.

D-22 (owner veto): our own licence proprietary, all rights reserved to the owner, until the owner chooses (§17.3); no dependency may constrain the choice. Rejected: leaving it undecided; an open licence by default. Cost: low (a licence file) until code is published.
notes: Owner-rule tension: OWNER-INSTRUCTIONS records the owner's intent to make this module GPL-3 (not reflected here).

statement: D-23: deterministic transcendentals through dmath (our TypeScript port of fdlibm 5.3 with Sun's notice) with an allowlist lint (exact Math members only; ** only with literal exponents 0–4, rewritten to multiplications; ratio() for computed divisors) that also scans vendored dependencies. Rejected: in-house polynomial approximations; trusting Math.*; the @stdlib packages (94-package closure). Cost: low.

D-24: goldens are stage-isolated (new stage code on frozen upstream outputs) and built at M1; end-to-end goldens re-signed only with a cascade record; every milestone files its declared shifts; a same-seed output change is never let ride silently. Rejected: one whole-model hash per seed; goldens at M4. Cost: trivial.

D-25: the evolution hook in the base is exactly one built and tested path — add a growth stage to an existing town, with wall → ring road as a typed conversion — plus the epoch key component and the transformation-event vocabulary (decline included); the evolution engine is staged by the owner with interfaces concrete (§4.11). Rejected: no incremental path; the full engine now. Cost: low.
D-26: identity = opaque lineage-hash addresses with survival and succession (§6.3). Rejected: hierarchical creation-order ids; per-kind counters. Cost: high after M1.
D-27: work limits, never wall clock, bound every output-affecting budget (§5.1). Rejected: wall-clock watchdogs. Cost: low.

D-28: the model digest is a Merkle root over the eager model's content only, maintained at batch commit (§6.2) (canonical serialisation costs ≈ 1.2 s per CITY model; provenance must not move goldens). Rejected: hashing the canonical serialisation per batch. Cost: high after M1.

D-29: the clean-room chain (§17.1): implementers read only this document and a checked digest; the product in its own repository plat/ with a path rule; reference numbers only through committed numbers-only files (baselines.json and the D-5 panel's ftg-captures.json and ng-counts.json); a hashed deny-list scan in CI and a palette audit per milestone; reference-derived constants labelled by origin; a seat ledger in CLEAN-ROOM.md. Rejected: findings and captures as implementer inputs; path-only CI rules. Cost: low (process), in place before M0's code.
notes: Part of conflict SCOPE-C02 (VS5-3): omits record.json.

statement: D-30: every threshold has a number now — reference-settable bands by §13.5's band rule; thresholds no reference can set in §13.7, each with a provisional number, the first confirming milestone and a pre-decided fallback; no placeholder can gate or pass. Rejected: placeholders set by the corpus phase. Cost: trivial.

D-31 (owner veto): matched references TOWN = MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN (≈ 5 600); CITY = MFCG size 80 and FTG BIG_CITY (24 500); METROPOLIS = MFCG size 130; FTG's premium METROPOLIS is not purchased — the METROPOLIS side-by-side uses MFCG 130 with FTG's published metropolis pictures as an unscored reference card; a one-month premium FTG subscription for one measured capture is the owner's option. Rejected: CITY-only FTG comparison; a purchase by the program. Cost: low (one capture day if the owner buys).

D-32 (owner veto: new capability rather than repair): economy (resource chains, items and services with prices, stock per building, global price edits), personality (trait sentences, motivation, mannerism, hobbies), education gated by class and a stat block with profession modifiers are @plat/sim content (M4b), derived from their keys with our own authored tables; schema stubs in the base (§10.3); the stat block a named game-system pack off by default (D-3); the family-tree view in the app (§14). Rejected: leaving them unrecorded; putting them on the one-click path. Cost: low (dropping it removes ≈ 2–4 pw from M4b).

D-33: the two ladders meet at 1 500 inhabitants (village THORP → HAMLET → VILLAGE ends there; TOWN band 1 500–10 000 starts there); size within a rung follows population; per-rung rows in ladder.json (§1.1); a request below 1 500 routes to the village product (clamped and reported while none is registered); one above 120 000 is clamped and reported. Rejected: an undefined boundary; a 2 000 floor leaving a gap. Cost: trivial.

D-34: three CI tiers with wall-clock budgets (PR ≤ 15 min, nightly ≤ 4 h, milestone ≤ 12 h) on a stated runner; the oracle once per sequence; an over-budget job is split, never re-capped (§13.8). Rejected: one full run per change. Cost: trivial.

D-35: build order M-1 → M0 → M1 viewable town → M2a editing core → M2b parity (second preset; METROPOLIS measured and tuned) → M3a full editing, migration and API → M3b exports, forms and should-have tiers → M4 hardening and the incremental path → M4b content module → M5 stage 2; nothing leaves the program (M3 was overloaded, ≈ 31–40 pw itemised against 20–26; the module needs the relation store first). Rejected: lit before editing; moving exports, forms or the module out. Cost: low.

statement: J-R1: Chose a columnar, transferable mark table over `Mark[]` objects — because a 60 000-object list costs the receiving thread ≈ 140 ms to deserialise while typed arrays transfer in constant time and slice cheaply into deltas (§8.1).
J-R2: Chose world-aligned tile rasters over per-district rasters — because district boundaries are streets and a district bitmap cannot follow continuous zoom (§8.1).
J-R3: Chose low-chroma value steps over saturated hues for the default roles — because the restraint clause asks for one ink and a few roles, and eight tones meet every contrast floor (§8.2).

J-R4: Chose Canvas2D as `lit`'s reference backend over WebGL2 — because one drawing path keeps screen, PNG and print identical, removes the duplicate render path both creators warned about, and every part of the lit look has a vector …

J-R5: Chose the ground tone over kerb hairlines as the city band's figure-ground — because a kerb line doubles the linework at city zoom and fights the casing idiom; hairlines are the pre-decided fallback (§8.5).

J-R6: Chose not to draw avenue trees at the city band over a thin green line inside the corridor — because at city zoom a corridor is ≈ 2 px, where a line fuses with the casing and adds a ninth tone (§8.5).

J-R7: Chose no S9 preview over a block preview — because §12.5's laws hold the one-second bar without one for every TOWN and CITY and for METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings, the slower first map above is …

J-R8: Chose settling on exact 2^¼ zoom stops over re-rastering at arbitrary scales — because an arbitrary-scale raster defeats the cache and the per-stop label placement; the settled scale is within ± 9 % of the requested one (§8.8).
J-R9: Chose Canvas2D glyphs composed onto the tiles over SDF text — because once tiles are composited text never needs the GPU, and one text path keeps text identical on every output (§8.9).

J-R10: Chose a handle-and-tiles worker boundary over sending the document or mark objects to the main thread — because structured-cloning a CITY entity table costs ≈ 162 ms and a 60 000-mark list ≈ 140 ms, while bitmaps and typed arrays transfer in constant time (§8.9).

J-R11: Chose stamped, ranked scatter tiles over per-entity Bridson sampling — because sampling costs ≈ 12 µs per tree while a stamp costs under 1 µs, and ranked tiles give every band a subset of the finer band by construction …

J-R12: Chose label placement as view data measured with our own font metrics over placement in the model — because collisions change with zoom inside a band, and over the host's text engine, because engines shape text differently (§9.1).

J-R13: Chose a minimal own emblem generator plus import over import only and over a full blazon engine — because the legend should carry an emblem in one click at a fraction of a person-week and heraldic depth is not a map-parity item (§9.5).

J-R14: Chose to build CityJSON over leaving it for later — because its integer-vertex-plus-transform encoding carries our centimetre lattice losslessly, so the exporter is thin, and it gives GIS users a standard 3-D path (§11.1).
notes: CityJSON built; contradicts §0.6 history "CityJSON to the deferrals" (SCOPE-C10).

statement: J-R15: Chose host-as-store over a sync service of our own — because the product is a standalone, backend-free library, a host already owns accounts and storage, and §11.3's protocol makes any host a correct store (§11.5).

J-R16: Chose a transport-agnostic bridge plus the static VTT exports over a Roll20 extension — because an extension needs an account and store publishing outside a standalone program, and FTG's extension only relays the same messages (§11.5).

J-R17: Chose a per-building cost of ≈ 58–75 µs at p95 over matching MFCG's 12–39 µs — because PLAT builds what MFCG does not, which D-7 ranks above speed; the first map stays under one second for every TOWN and CITY request and for METROPOLIS up …
notes: Per-building cost ≈ 58–75 µs vs MFCG 12–39 µs; relates to SCOPE-C01.; Review-id citations (history): D-7, NR3-5

statement: J-R18: Chose the derivation pool as the primary configuration over a single worker — because after the eager allocation the per-district stages are pure functions of eager upstream state and their own sub-streams, so they run in parallel without shared writes; M1 and …

J-R19: Chose the low 64 bits of the entity key — the seed key mixed with the lineage hash, layer and island — as the one key of every render-time hash over the bare lineage hash, the address and the interned handle — because the lineage alone carries no seed and would repeat the same looks at the same derivation positions in every town (VD2-6), the entity key is what every stream …

J-R20: Chose a slot-major draw order with passes inside each slot over the pass-major order — because pass-major drew every road casing over masses, fields, woods and shadows against the slot table's reasons, while separate casing and body slots keep GEO-28's guarantee (§8.1; N-7).

J-R21: Chose composing base and labels into one bitmap per tile in the tile worker over two tile layers committed to the main thread — because it halves first-paint commits and per-frame draws at the same memory while a label change still never re-rasters the map (§8.8; N-5).

J-R22: Chose a canvas budget derived from the viewport (3P + 7 MB) with tier ceilings and a tile-DPR step-down over fixed per-tier numbers — because the fixed low and mid budgets could not hold their own worst-case views (§8.8; N-9).

J-R23: Chose to run every model-reading render step — live-layer providers, override resolution, on-demand bands, `compose()`, close-ups — where the model is, and to give the tile worker display-list tables only, over a model replica in the tile worker — because a replica doubles the working set and must follow every edit (§8.9; N-4).

J-R24: Chose to apply an instance override by ordinal only while the entity's lineage and the ordinal's position both hold over applying it whenever the address survives — because a carried successor keeps the address but not the lineage, so the same ordinal lands on another tree (§8.10; NF-D11).

J-R25: Chose bit-reversal (van der Corput) ranks for jittered grids and lines over a second blue-noise ranking — because the rank is then a pure function of the ordinal and as stable as it (§8.10; N-10).

J-R26: Chose pins fixed at their own and finer stops and yielding at coarser ones over pins fixed at every stop — because a pixel-sized pin grows in world units as the view zooms out and would collide there (§9.2; N-28).

J-R27: Chose to decide the quarter-tree rung from geometry before the greedy, with one ancestor candidate per stop, over letting it arise from collisions inside the greedy — because the local evaluation needs every candidate's place in the strict order fixed in advance (§9.2, §9.4; N-11).

J-R28: Chose `ground` as the one fallback halo role, and darker inks for `lit` and `hatched`, over per-family halo roles and lower floors — because the matrix already guarantees ink against ground in every accepted palette and outlines over masses need the separation (§8.2, §9.4; N-3).

J-R29: Chose to draw `ink`'s walls in the ink and its courts as ground at the city band over a ninth city-band tone — because the restraint clause names one ink and 4–8 roles and an enclosed court's small step adds noise at city zoom (§8.2, §8.5; N-25).

J-R30: Chose a bounded random-style repair — fixed row order, ≤ 100 steps, ≤ 3 draws, then the shipped palette — over the unbounded raise — because only a bounded procedure can promise that every presented style meets the floors (§8.2; N-26).

J-R31: Chose a strict WGS84 GeoJSON by an inverse transverse Mercator at a documented default anchor, plus a metric file by prior arrangement, over a local metric CRS with a `crs` member — because the latter fails RFC 7946 and is read by GIS tools as degrees (§11.1; N-14).
J-R32: Chose glyph outlines as SVG's default text over embedded text, keeping the embedded face as an option — because only outlines draw the same glyphs in every consumer (§11.1; N-13).

J-R33: Chose fate confirmation by token and fate equality (or resubmission with fates filled) over a force flag — because the committed event must carry exactly the fates and renames the user saw (§11.2; NF-D14, VD4-4).

J-R34: Chose a per-viewer `stylePreset` view key over treating the canonical style as a last-writer-wins view key — because a viewer's look must neither rewrite the shared style nor silently diverge from it (§11.3; N-15).

J-R35: Chose first-map budgets as laws of the building count, with the one-second knee and the miss above it declared, over one bar per rung — because size follows population inside a rung (§12.5; N-2).

J-R36: Chose to state load verification as a law of the log (V = M(B) + Σ c(e) + S14 + 5 ms) over saving checkpoints — because checkpoints would multiply edit-heavy documents while the wait is already off the path to the picture (§12.6; N-16).

J-R37: Chose to let a CI font test pick each face's small-caps and figure path — the face's features, the family's OFL SC cut, then synthesis — over assuming the GSUB features — because nothing in the project shows the default face carries them (§9.2; N-12).

J-R38: Chose to read O3 (d)'s model-time bars over every size a rung builds and to declare where they hold — p95 up to ≈ 4 500 / 17 700 / 58 800 people, the max (each generation ≤ 1.25 × its own law) up to ≈ 3 400 / 13 600 / 45 800 — and the miss above them for the owner's veto, over reading them at the targets only — because size follows population inside a rung, as N-2 ruled for the first map, and a reading at the targets hides the miss; and chose to judge the max …

statement: J-R39: Chose explicit passes on `OrderSlot` with most-specific-wins resolution and refusal of any unresolved or tied (semantic, pass), with `derived` entries for the raised under-copy and projected shadows, over one slot per semantic or an order fixed in code — because a way's casing and body must sit in different slots while sheets stay data (§8.2; NR-3).

J-R40: Chose furniture-placement and snap queries answered by the tile worker within one frame — the first class of its queue, served between the steps of resumable raster jobs (`TileBackend.begin` → `RasterJob.step(8)`) — over copying mark kinds and vertices into the main thread's hit-test slices or placing furniture in the generation worker — because the slices would carry model-sized geometry and the generation worker's index has no kinds, vertices or placed labels; and chose the resumable job over a synchronous raster call …

J-R41: Chose a transient display list built in the generation worker for SVG exports and released after writing, over handing SVG to the tile worker or keeping a second resident list — because the SVG writer reads the document, which the tile worker never holds, and exports are occasional (§11.1, §12.8; NR-5).

J-R42: Chose a constant stream key for the stamp-tile library — (class, reference spacing, creation index: 0–3 for the four tiles, 4 for their shared border band), `STAGE_VIEW`, `render.stampTiles` — with integer-centimetre points, `dmath` transcendentals, index-order sums and ties and the stated removal update, built when the product is built by `plat/tools/stamptiles/` and shipped as a hash-checked asset, over a seed- or document-keyed library and over building it in each session — because the tiles are shared by every document, session and host, the per-town variety comes from the stamp's offset, rotation, spacing and seed-dependent variant, and a session build ran …

J-R43: Chose a declared PLAT CityJSON Extension for `+platGeoAnchor`, validated in CI against the repository's schema, over a sidecar as the primary, with a `<name>.geoanchor.json` sidecar as the pre-decided fallback — because the extension keeps the anchor inside the one file a GIS user moves around and the sidecar leaves the CityJSON file valid by construction (§11.1; NR-7).

J-R44: Chose to keep the derivation pool primary at each size where it runs within its law + 10 %, measures faster than a single worker on the same generations and gives identical digests for pool sizes 0–3 — each size range otherwise running the configuration faster at the nearest measured size — over one bar of p95 ≤ 300 ms at the CITY target — because the pooled law itself puts the default CITY request at 265–340 ms, so that bar would have replaced the pool by a single worker ≈ 85–115 ms slower …

statement: J-R45: Chose a pin pass at placement time — a stop's pins in `moveLabel` order, a pin meeting an earlier fixed pin hidden at that stop and reported — with `moveLabel`'s refusal kept as the interactive guard, over refusing the warps, renames, rerolls and style changes that bring pins together — because those edits are not about labels and must not be blocked by one, while hiding a pin is a reported view change; and chose `moveLabel` order over priority …

J-R48: Chose one set of four stamp tiles per class at a reference spacing of 4 m, scaled per entity by its spacing ÷ 4 m, over a set per (class, spacing) — because the spacing is drawn per entity in whole centimetres, so a per-spacing library has hundreds of members per class (≈ 19 ms each to build, megabytes as an …

J-R50: Chose four seam-compatible stamp tiles per class sharing one border band — the points within half the reference spacing of a tile edge, cut from a fifth, full toroidal tile, each tile filling the rest by Bridson seeded with the band — over the independent variants (3.5–5 pairs of trees per 64-m seam closer than the spacing), over one larger toroidal tile (every instance position repeats on a periodic lattice), over a band of the full spacing (≈ 23 % of each cell's points repeated instead of ≈ 12 %) and over a band sampled by Bridson inside itself (a density stripe along every lattice line) — because the half-width cut band gives 0 close pairs across every seam for every band's subset (measured on all 256 2 × 2 arrangements) while keeping ≈ 88 % …

J-R52: Chose integer-centimetre instance positions computed with `dmath` (R_θ from the integer `rotationCdeg`), the whole instance function under §6.5's allowlist lint, over double positions from the engine's `Math.cos` — because the model-format exporters write those positions and promise files byte-identical on every host, and the centimetre is the model's own lattice, so the face test is exact too; …

J-R53: Chose, for a PNG time miss, the None row filter on every row on every host — then zlib level 3 in Node, and in browsers, whose `CompressionStream` takes no level, the D-18 re-declaration — over zlib level 3 alone, which browsers cannot apply and which measured the smaller lever, and over a fixed Sub filter, which measured slower and larger than None on flat, relief and textured synthetic maps; and kept the per-row minimum-sum rule as the default — because it gives the smallest file wherever rows carry gradients or texture (§8.8, §12.7; NR4-4).

J-R54: Chose a light step — the path sun quantised to 15° of azimuth and 5° of altitude — for `faceLight`, the two-tone roofs, `hillshade` and the `lit` crown bake, keying the `under` and `over` layers (or `base`) by it and re-rastering them in a light pass that runs to completion, over lighting them by the 1° sun (a full re-raster per 1° step) and over keying only the shadows by the sun (roofs and crowns of several suns side by side, differing by tier); the fallback holds the fixed sun for all but the shadows (§8.4, §8.8, §8.10, §12.7; NR4-5).

J-S10: Chose a proprietary default licence over leaving the licence undecided or defaulting to an open licence — because it keeps every option for the owner (DEF-14; D-22).
